# Local-only generations as worker task inputs

Read CLAUDE.md at the repo root first — it has cross-cutting rules and points to relevant sub-docs (especially `task_worker_lifecycle.md`, `unified_task_creation.md`, `storage_uploads.md`, `edge_functions.md`).

## Background

The app now supports `storage_mode='local'` generations (see `src/shared/lib/media/createGenerationFromFile.ts` → `createGenerationForLocalFile()`). The bytes live in the user's browser via a `FileSystemFileHandle` persisted in IndexedDB; the DB row carries `local_handle_id` instead of a `location` URL.

Today, when a user takes a generation and uses it as **input** to a worker task (travel, refine, masked-edit, etc.), the app puts a Supabase Storage URL into task params and the worker fetches it via HTTP. For local-only generations, that URL doesn't exist — and the worker has no way to reach into the browser.

This task wires those local-only generations through to the worker correctly, with a tiered strategy.

## Design

Implement a **per-input** resolution layer that runs at task-create time. For each input that references a generation:

1. If `storage_mode === 'remote'` (or absent / 'uploading' that has materialized) → use existing URL behavior. No change.
2. If `storage_mode === 'local'`:
   - **Detect whether a local worker is reachable** via a healthcheck (e.g. `GET http://localhost:<configured-port>/health` with a short timeout, ~250ms). Cache the answer for the duration of the task-creation call (don't re-probe per input).
   - **If local worker reachable**: read the file bytes from the FileSystemFileHandle, write them to a known shared dir (e.g. `~/.reigh-local-files/<local_handle_id>.<ext>`), and put a `file://` URL pointing at that path into the task params. The worker's `download_utils.py` already handles `file://` URLs (verify this — `reigh-worker/source/utils/download_utils.py` around line 60), so no worker changes should be needed. The materialized file is the "duplicate" per user wording.
   - **If no local worker**: upload the file bytes to Supabase Storage on demand. Reuse the existing upload helper in `src/shared/lib/media/imageUploader.ts`. Put the resulting public URL into task params. Mark the generation row with the new `location` (or a sibling `materialized_location`) so a second use of the same input doesn't re-upload — idempotent.

## Mixed inputs

A single task can reference both local-only and remote generations as inputs. The resolver MUST operate per-input, not per-task. After resolution, the task params contain a uniform set of URL strings (mix of `https://...` and `file://...`) — the worker doesn't know or care which inputs were originally local.

## Cleanup ("delete the duplicate after")

After task completion, the duplicate created during resolution must be cleaned up so we don't accumulate orphaned copies:

- **Local-worker `file://` materialization**: when the task completes, the file at `~/.reigh-local-files/<handle_id>.<ext>` is no longer needed. Delete it. Implement this in the `complete_task` edge function path OR via a worker-side cleanup hook OR via an app-side post-completion handler — whichever is most natural given the existing complete-task lifecycle. The original FileSystemFileHandle in the browser is untouched; we only delete the materialized copy.
- **Remote-worker upload-on-demand**: this is more nuanced. If we keep the uploaded copy, the generation effectively becomes remote-mode, defeating the user's local choice. Recommended: keep the upload only for the duration of the task (idempotency caching) and delete it after task completion. Update the generation row to remove the cached URL. Same lifecycle hook as above. If the user uses the same local generation as input again later, we re-upload (small cost, preserves intent).

The lifecycle hook should look at the resolved task params, identify which entries were materializations of local generations (mark them at creation time so cleanup knows), and clean each up. Don't touch generations that were natively remote.

## Detection of local worker

The localhost healthcheck endpoint and port: check existing reigh-worker server entrypoint (`reigh-worker/source/runtime/worker/server.py`) for the actual healthcheck route + port. If none exists, you'll need to add a tiny `/health` endpoint to the worker (returns 200 OK + JSON `{ok:true}`). Keep this minimal.

The app also needs to know which port to probe — read it from an env var (`VITE_LOCAL_WORKER_HEALTHCHECK_URL` or similar), default to a sensible value. Don't hard-code.

If the healthcheck fails (timeout, connection refused), fall back to remote behavior. Don't surface an error to the user — silent fallback is correct UX.

## Where to put the resolution layer

There's a unified task-creation path in `src/shared/lib/tasks/`. Look for the common entry point (probably a hook like `useCreateTask` or a shared `createTask` helper). The resolver should run there, immediately before the create-task edge function call. Sub-doc `unified_task_creation.md` is authoritative — read it first.

For tasks that build their own params (e.g. `src/shared/lib/tasks/travelBetweenImages/segmentImages.ts`, `src/shared/lib/tasks/imageEditing/buildMaskedEditTaskParams.ts`), the resolver needs a hook into each. Consider whether the resolver runs at the very end of param assembly (one place to plug in) or whether each task builder calls it explicitly. The first option is simpler and harder to forget.

## What NOT to do

- Do NOT make the worker do FileSystemFileHandle deserialization. Browser handles can't cross processes.
- Do NOT eagerly upload all local files at drop time. That defeats the point — only materialize on USE.
- Do NOT add a "this will be uploaded to cloud, OK?" prompt. The fallback should be silent. (We can add UX later if needed.)
- Do NOT refactor the unified task-creation system. Plug into it.
- Do NOT add comments explaining the change. The diff speaks for itself.

## Tests

- Add tests for the resolver covering: all-remote inputs (passthrough), all-local + local worker present (file:// path), all-local + remote only (upload + cache), mixed inputs (per-input branching), cleanup after completion.
- Mock the healthcheck and the upload helper. Don't hit real network.
- Mirror existing test patterns in `src/shared/lib/tasks/__tests__/` or wherever co-located tests live.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` — must not introduce new errors beyond pre-existing patterns.
- `npx vitest run` for affected directories.
- Manually trace through one task type (travel-between-images is a good one) to verify the resolver runs and the URL contract holds.

## Deliverables

- The per-input resolver, wired into the unified task-creation path.
- Local-worker healthcheck utility.
- Cleanup hook on task completion.
- A `/health` endpoint on the worker if one doesn't exist.
- Tests covering the matrix above.

(flagged 2 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the actual export surface in `supabase/functions/ai-timeline-agent/llm/messages.ts` and its consumers. step 6 says to 'remove local `isrecord`' from `messages.ts` and import it from `utils.ts`, but without also preserving `messages.ts` as an exporter or rewiring `index.ts`, `db.ts`, `tool-calls.ts`, and `selectedclips.ts`, that change would break the module graph immediately. (flagged 2 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the render-gating cleanup plan against remotion's runtime exports in `node_modules/remotion/dist/cjs/cancel-render.js:46-70`. `cancelrender()` stores an error and throws to abort the render; it is not a benign cleanup for an abandoned `delayrender` handle, so step 2's instruction to call `cancelrender(handle)` on unmount is technically wrong and would abort preview or export with an error. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked how remotion itself acquires delay handles in `node_modules/remotion/dist/cjs/iframe.js:8-18`. remotion's own components create the handle synchronously with `usestate(() => delayrender(...))`; the plan says 'calls delayrender() on mount', which reads like an effect-time action and leaves the initial-frame blocking behavior underspecified compared with the actual library pattern. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the new `useaudioparam()` sketch against `src/tools/video-editor/effects/compileeffect.tsx:1-2`. the plan defines it in terms of `interpolate(audio[binding.source], ...)` but does not explicitly import `interpolate` into the new hook file or simplify it to straight arithmetic, so the helper's implementation contract is still looser than it needs to be. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked revised step 2.4 against `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useclipresize.ts:76-100`. the plan still says to clamp audio by writing back to `action.end`, but the current hook treats the callback `action` as input data and then creates fresh row actions from it. mutating that caller-owned object is unnecessary and risks coupling the resize hook to outside references instead of using a local `clampedend` variable. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the no-duration-fetch decision against `src/tools/travel-between-images/hooks/video/useshotfinalvideos.ts:19-37`, `src/tools/video-editor/lib/config-utils.ts:17-35`, and `src/tools/video-editor/compositions/visualclip.tsx:114-123`. the repository still derives clip length from `to - from`, and the final-video query still provides no duration metadata, so the revised plan still cannot prove that `to: endtime - starttime` is safe for shorter source media; a short final video can still be asked to play longer than its actual content. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the hand-built replacement clip against the existing insert path in `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useassetmanagement.ts:201-252,262-271` and serialization in `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/usetimelinecommit.ts:210-216`. the revised `timelineeditor` sketch still bypasses current insertion invariants such as manual-track geometry defaults and explicit `cliporder` updates, so replacement clips on manual visual tracks will not be initialized the same way as other inserted video clips and may serialize in a different per-track order. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)

        Idea:
# Local-only generations as worker task inputs

Read CLAUDE.md at the repo root first — it has cross-cutting rules and points to relevant sub-docs (especially `task_worker_lifecycle.md`, `unified_task_creation.md`, `storage_uploads.md`, `edge_functions.md`).

## Background

The app now supports `storage_mode='local'` generations (see `src/shared/lib/media/createGenerationFromFile.ts` → `createGenerationForLocalFile()`). The bytes live in the user's browser via a `FileSystemFileHandle` persisted in IndexedDB; the DB row carries `local_handle_id` instead of a `location` URL.

Today, when a user takes a generation and uses it as **input** to a worker task (travel, refine, masked-edit, etc.), the app puts a Supabase Storage URL into task params and the worker fetches it via HTTP. For local-only generations, that URL doesn't exist — and the worker has no way to reach into the browser.

This task wires those local-only generations through to the worker correctly, with a tiered strategy.

## Design

Implement a **per-input** resolution layer that runs at task-create time. For each input that references a generation:

1. If `storage_mode === 'remote'` (or absent / 'uploading' that has materialized) → use existing URL behavior. No change.
2. If `storage_mode === 'local'`:
   - **Detect whether a local worker is reachable** via a healthcheck (e.g. `GET http://localhost:<configured-port>/health` with a short timeout, ~250ms). Cache the answer for the duration of the task-creation call (don't re-probe per input).
   - **If local worker reachable**: read the file bytes from the FileSystemFileHandle, write them to a known shared dir (e.g. `~/.reigh-local-files/<local_handle_id>.<ext>`), and put a `file://` URL pointing at that path into the task params. The worker's `download_utils.py` already handles `file://` URLs (verify this — `reigh-worker/source/utils/download_utils.py` around line 60), so no worker changes should be needed. The materialized file is the "duplicate" per user wording.
   - **If no local worker**: upload the file bytes to Supabase Storage on demand. Reuse the existing upload helper in `src/shared/lib/media/imageUploader.ts`. Put the resulting public URL into task params. Mark the generation row with the new `location` (or a sibling `materialized_location`) so a second use of the same input doesn't re-upload — idempotent.

## Mixed inputs

A single task can reference both local-only and remote generations as inputs. The resolver MUST operate per-input, not per-task. After resolution, the task params contain a uniform set of URL strings (mix of `https://...` and `file://...`) — the worker doesn't know or care which inputs were originally local.

## Cleanup ("delete the duplicate after")

After task completion, the duplicate created during resolution must be cleaned up so we don't accumulate orphaned copies:

- **Local-worker `file://` materialization**: when the task completes, the file at `~/.reigh-local-files/<handle_id>.<ext>` is no longer needed. Delete it. Implement this in the `complete_task` edge function path OR via a worker-side cleanup hook OR via an app-side post-completion handler — whichever is most natural given the existing complete-task lifecycle. The original FileSystemFileHandle in the browser is untouched; we only delete the materialized copy.
- **Remote-worker upload-on-demand**: this is more nuanced. If we keep the uploaded copy, the generation effectively becomes remote-mode, defeating the user's local choice. Recommended: keep the upload only for the duration of the task (idempotency caching) and delete it after task completion. Update the generation row to remove the cached URL. Same lifecycle hook as above. If the user uses the same local generation as input again later, we re-upload (small cost, preserves intent).

The lifecycle hook should look at the resolved task params, identify which entries were materializations of local generations (mark them at creation time so cleanup knows), and clean each up. Don't touch generations that were natively remote.

## Detection of local worker

The localhost healthcheck endpoint and port: check existing reigh-worker server entrypoint (`reigh-worker/source/runtime/worker/server.py`) for the actual healthcheck route + port. If none exists, you'll need to add a tiny `/health` endpoint to the worker (returns 200 OK + JSON `{ok:true}`). Keep this minimal.

The app also needs to know which port to probe — read it from an env var (`VITE_LOCAL_WORKER_HEALTHCHECK_URL` or similar), default to a sensible value. Don't hard-code.

If the healthcheck fails (timeout, connection refused), fall back to remote behavior. Don't surface an error to the user — silent fallback is correct UX.

## Where to put the resolution layer

There's a unified task-creation path in `src/shared/lib/tasks/`. Look for the common entry point (probably a hook like `useCreateTask` or a shared `createTask` helper). The resolver should run there, immediately before the create-task edge function call. Sub-doc `unified_task_creation.md` is authoritative — read it first.

For tasks that build their own params (e.g. `src/shared/lib/tasks/travelBetweenImages/segmentImages.ts`, `src/shared/lib/tasks/imageEditing/buildMaskedEditTaskParams.ts`), the resolver needs a hook into each. Consider whether the resolver runs at the very end of param assembly (one place to plug in) or whether each task builder calls it explicitly. The first option is simpler and harder to forget.

## What NOT to do

- Do NOT make the worker do FileSystemFileHandle deserialization. Browser handles can't cross processes.
- Do NOT eagerly upload all local files at drop time. That defeats the point — only materialize on USE.
- Do NOT add a "this will be uploaded to cloud, OK?" prompt. The fallback should be silent. (We can add UX later if needed.)
- Do NOT refactor the unified task-creation system. Plug into it.
- Do NOT add comments explaining the change. The diff speaks for itself.

## Tests

- Add tests for the resolver covering: all-remote inputs (passthrough), all-local + local worker present (file:// path), all-local + remote only (upload + cache), mixed inputs (per-input branching), cleanup after completion.
- Mock the healthcheck and the upload helper. Don't hit real network.
- Mirror existing test patterns in `src/shared/lib/tasks/__tests__/` or wherever co-located tests live.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` — must not introduce new errors beyond pre-existing patterns.
- `npx vitest run` for affected directories.
- Manually trace through one task type (travel-between-images is a good one) to verify the resolver runs and the URL contract holds.

## Deliverables

- The per-input resolver, wired into the unified task-creation path.
- Local-worker healthcheck utility.
- Cleanup hook on task completion.
- A `/health` endpoint on the worker if one doesn't exist.
- Tests covering the matrix above.

```
124	export async function fetchTaskContext(

126	  taskId: string,
127	  logger?: CompletionLogger,
128	): Promise<TaskContext | null> {
129	  const { data: task, error } = await supabase
130	    .from("tasks")
131	    .select(`id, task_type, project_id, params, result_data, task_types!tasks_task_type_fkey(tool_type, category, content_type, variant_type)`)
132	    .eq("id", taskId)

134	
135	  if (error || !task) {
136	    logger?.error('Failed to fetch task context', {
137	      task_id: taskId,

139	    });
140	    return null;
141	  }
142	
143	  const taskTypeInfo = task.task_types || {};
144	
145	  return {
146	    id: task.id,
```

```json
  "content": "import { getLocalWorkerConfig } from './config';\n\nexport interface IngestResult {\n  fileUrl: string;\n  cleanupPath: string;\n}\n\nexport interface IngestOptions {\n  generationId: string;\n  signal?: AbortSignal;\n}\n\nexport async function ingestFileToLocalWorker(\n  file: File,\n  { generationId, signal }: IngestOptions,\n): Promise<IngestResult> {\n  const { baseUrl } = getLocalWorkerConfig();\n  const formData = new FormData();\n  formData.append('generation_id', generationId);\n  formData.append('file', file);\n\n  const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/ingest`, {\n    method: 'POST',\n    body: formData,\n    signal,\n  });\n\n  if (!response.ok) {\n    throw new Error(`Local worker /ingest returned HTTP ${response.status}`);\n  }\n\n  const payload = (await response.json()) as { path?: unknown };\n  if (typeof payload.path !== 'string' || payload.path.length === 0) {\n    throw new Error('Local worker /ingest response missing string `path`');\n  }\n\n  return {\n    fileUrl: `file://${payload.path}`,\n    cleanupPath: payload.path,\n  };\n}\n\nexport async function requestLocalWorkerCleanup(path: string): Promise<void> {\n  const { baseUrl } = getLocalWorkerConfig();\n  try {\n    await fetch(`${baseUrl}/cleanup`, {\n      method: 'POST',\n      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n      body: JSON.stringify({ path }),\n    });\n  } catch (error) {\n    console.error('[LocalWorkerCleanup] failed for path', path, error);\n  }\n}\n"
}
```

```json
  "content": "import type { SupabaseClient } from 'https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2.49.4';\nimport { toErrorMessage } from '../_shared/errorMessage.ts';\nimport type {\n  CompletionFollowUpIssue,\n  MaterializedInputRecord,\n  TaskContext,\n} from './completionHelpers.ts';\nimport { cleanupFile } from './storage.ts';\nimport type { CompletionLogger } from './types.ts';\n\nfunction isMaterializedInputRecord(value: unknown): value is MaterializedInputRecord {\n  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object') return false;\n  const r = value as Record<string, unknown>;\n  return (\n    typeof r.generation_id === 'string' &&\n    (r.kind === 'file' || r.kind === 'remote') &&\n    typeof r.target === 'string'\n  );\n}\n\nexport async function cleanupMaterializedInputs(\n  supabaseAdmin: SupabaseClient,\n  taskContext: TaskContext,\n  logger?: CompletionLogger,\n): Promise<CompletionFollowUpIssue[]> {\n  const raw = taskContext.materialized_inputs;\n  if (!raw || !Array.isArray(raw) || raw.length === 0) {\n    return [];\n  }\n\n  const issues: CompletionFollowUpIssue[] = [];\n\n  for (const record of raw) {\n    if (!isMaterializedInputRecord(record)) {\n      issues.push({\n        step: 'materialized_input_cleanup',\n        code: 'materialized_input_cleanup_failed',\n        message: `Skipping malformed materialized_inputs entry: ${JSON.stringify(record)}`,\n      });\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    if (record.kind === 'file') {\n      logger?.info(\n        `[MaterializedInputCleanup] worker-side cleanup for path=${record.target}`,\n        { generation_id: record.generation_id },\n      );\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    try {\n      await cleanupFile(supabaseAdmin, record.target);\n    } catch (error) {\n      issues.push({\n        step: 'materialized_input_cleanup',\n        code: 'materialized_input_cleanup_failed',\n        message: `Failed to remove materialized remote target ${record.target}: ${toErrorMessage(error)}`,\n      });\n    }\n  }\n\n  return issues;\n}\n"
}
```

# Local-only generations as worker task inputs

Read CLAUDE.md at the repo root first — it has cross-cutting rules and points to relevant sub-docs (especially `task_worker_lifecycle.md`, `unified_task_creation.md`, `storage_uploads.md`, `edge_functions.md`).

## Background

The app now supports `storage_mode='local'` generations (see `src/shared/lib/media/createGenerationFromFile.ts` → `createGenerationForLocalFile()`). The bytes live in the user's browser via a `FileSystemFileHandle` persisted in IndexedDB; the DB row carries `local_handle_id` instead of a `location` URL.

Today, when a user takes a generation and uses it as **input** to a worker task (travel, refine, masked-edit, etc.), the app puts a Supabase Storage URL into task params and the worker fetches it via HTTP. For local-only generations, that URL doesn't exist — and the worker has no way to reach into the browser.

This task wires those local-only generations through to the worker correctly, with a tiered strategy.

## Design

Implement a **per-input** resolution layer that runs at task-create time. For each input that references a generation:

1. If `storage_mode === 'remote'` (or absent / 'uploading' that has materialized) → use existing URL behavior. No change.
2. If `storage_mode === 'local'`:
   - **Detect whether a local worker is reachable** via a healthcheck (e.g. `GET http://localhost:<configured-port>/health` with a short timeout, ~250ms). Cache the answer for the duration of the task-creation call (don't re-probe per input).
   - **If local worker reachable**: read the file bytes from the FileSystemFileHandle, write them to a known shared dir (e.g. `~/.reigh-local-files/<local_handle_id>.<ext>`), and put a `file://` URL pointing at that path into the task params. The worker's `download_utils.py` already handles `file://` URLs (verify this — `reigh-worker/source/utils/download_utils.py` around line 60), so no worker changes should be needed. The materialized file is the "duplicate" per user wording.
   - **If no local worker**: upload the file bytes to Supabase Storage on demand. Reuse the existing upload helper in `src/shared/lib/media/imageUploader.ts`. Put the resulting public URL into task params. Mark the generation row with the new `location` (or a sibling `materialized_location`) so a second use of the same input doesn't re-upload — idempotent.

## Mixed inputs

A single task can reference both local-only and remote generations as inputs. The resolver MUST operate per-input, not per-task. After resolution, the task params contain a uniform set of URL strings (mix of `https://...` and `file://...`) — the worker doesn't know or care which inputs were originally local.

## Cleanup ("delete the duplicate after")

After task completion, the duplicate created during resolution must be cleaned up so we don't accumulate orphaned copies:

- **Local-worker `file://` materialization**: when the task completes, the file at `~/.reigh-local-files/<handle_id>.<ext>` is no longer needed. Delete it. Implement this in the `complete_task` edge function path OR via a worker-side cleanup hook OR via an app-side post-completion handler — whichever is most natural given the existing complete-task lifecycle. The original FileSystemFileHandle in the browser is untouched; we only delete the materialized copy.
- **Remote-worker upload-on-demand**: this is more nuanced. If we keep the uploaded copy, the generation effectively becomes remote-mode, defeating the user's local choice. Recommended: keep the upload only for the duration of the task (idempotency caching) and delete it after task completion. Update the generation row to remove the cached URL. Same lifecycle hook as above. If the user uses the same local generation as input again later, we re-upload (small cost, preserves intent).

The lifecycle hook should look at the resolved task params, identify which entries were materializations of local generations (mark them at creation time so cleanup knows), and clean each up. Don't touch generations that were natively remote.

## Detection of local worker

The localhost healthcheck endpoint and port: check existing reigh-worker server entrypoint (`reigh-worker/source/runtime/worker/server.py`) for the actual healthcheck route + port. If none exists, you'll need to add a tiny `/health` endpoint to the worker (returns 200 OK + JSON `{ok:true}`). Keep this minimal.

The app also needs to know which port to probe — read it from an env var (`VITE_LOCAL_WORKER_HEALTHCHECK_URL` or similar), default to a sensible value. Don't hard-code.

If the healthcheck fails (timeout, connection refused), fall back to remote behavior. Don't surface an error to the user — silent fallback is correct UX.

## Where to put the resolution layer

There's a unified task-creation path in `src/shared/lib/tasks/`. Look for the common entry point (probably a hook like `useCreateTask` or a shared `createTask` helper). The resolver should run there, immediately before the create-task edge function call. Sub-doc `unified_task_creation.md` is authoritative — read it first.

For tasks that build their own params (e.g. `src/shared/lib/tasks/travelBetweenImages/segmentImages.ts`, `src/shared/lib/tasks/imageEditing/buildMaskedEditTaskParams.ts`), the resolver needs a hook into each. Consider whether the resolver runs at the very end of param assembly (one place to plug in) or whether each task builder calls it explicitly. The first option is simpler and harder to forget.

## What NOT to do

- Do NOT make the worker do FileSystemFileHandle deserialization. Browser handles can't cross processes.
- Do NOT eagerly upload all local files at drop time. That defeats the point — only materialize on USE.
- Do NOT add a "this will be uploaded to cloud, OK?" prompt. The fallback should be silent. (We can add UX later if needed.)
- Do NOT refactor the unified task-creation system. Plug into it.
- Do NOT add comments explaining the change. The diff speaks for itself.

## Tests

- Add tests for the resolver covering: all-remote inputs (passthrough), all-local + local worker present (file:// path), all-local + remote only (upload + cache), mixed inputs (per-input branching), cleanup after completion.
- Mock the healthcheck and the upload helper. Don't hit real network.
- Mirror existing test patterns in `src/shared/lib/tasks/__tests__/` or wherever co-located tests live.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` — must not introduce new errors beyond pre-existing patterns.
- `npx vitest run` for affected directories.
- Manually trace through one task type (travel-between-images is a good one) to verify the resolver runs and the URL contract holds.

## Deliverables

- The per-input resolver, wired into the unified task-creation path.
- Local-worker healthcheck utility.
- Cleanup hook on task completion.
- A `/health` endpoint on the worker if one doesn't exist.
- Tests covering the matrix above.
- Brief summary in your final message: every task type touched, every caller of the create-task path you verified.

(flagged 2 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the render-gating cleanup plan against remotion's runtime exports in `node_modules/remotion/dist/cjs/cancel-render.js:46-70`. `cancelrender()` stores an error and throws to abort the render; it is not a benign cleanup for an abandoned `delayrender` handle, so step 2's instruction to call `cancelrender(handle)` on unmount is technically wrong and would abort preview or export with an error. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked how remotion itself acquires delay handles in `node_modules/remotion/dist/cjs/iframe.js:8-18`. remotion's own components create the handle synchronously with `usestate(() => delayrender(...))`; the plan says 'calls delayrender() on mount', which reads like an effect-time action and leaves the initial-frame blocking behavior underspecified compared with the actual library pattern. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the new `useaudioparam()` sketch against `src/tools/video-editor/effects/compileeffect.tsx:1-2`. the plan defines it in terms of `interpolate(audio[binding.source], ...)` but does not explicitly import `interpolate` into the new hook file or simplify it to straight arithmetic, so the helper's implementation contract is still looser than it needs to be. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked revised step 2.4 against `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useclipresize.ts:76-100`. the plan still says to clamp audio by writing back to `action.end`, but the current hook treats the callback `action` as input data and then creates fresh row actions from it. mutating that caller-owned object is unnecessary and risks coupling the resize hook to outside references instead of using a local `clampedend` variable. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the no-duration-fetch decision against `src/tools/travel-between-images/hooks/video/useshotfinalvideos.ts:19-37`, `src/tools/video-editor/lib/config-utils.ts:17-35`, and `src/tools/video-editor/compositions/visualclip.tsx:114-123`. the repository still derives clip length from `to - from`, and the final-video query still provides no duration metadata, so the revised plan still cannot prove that `to: endtime - starttime` is safe for shorter source media; a short final video can still be asked to play longer than its actual content.   "content": "import { probeLocalWorker } from '@/shared/lib/localWorker/healthcheck';\n\nexport type MaterializedInputKind = 'file' | 'remote';\n\nexport interface MaterializedInputRecord {\n  generation_id: string;\n  kind: MaterializedInputKind;\n  target: string;\n}\n\nexport interface LocalWorkerSession {\n  probe(): Promise<boolean>;\n  register(record: MaterializedInputRecord): void;\n  records(): MaterializedInputRecord[];\n  cached(generationId: string): MaterializedInputRecord | null;\n}\n\nexport function beginLocalWorkerSession(): LocalWorkerSession {\n  let probePromise: Promise<boolean> | null = null;\n  const accumulated: MaterializedInputRecord[] = [];\n  const byGenerationId = new Map<string, MaterializedInputRecord>();\n\n  return {\n    probe(): Promise<boolean> {\n      if (!probePromise) {\n        probePromise = probeLocalWorker();\n      }\n      return probePromise;\n    },\n    register(record: MaterializedInputRecord): void {\n      const existing = byGenerationId.get(record.generation_id);\n      if (existing) return;\n      byGenerationId.set(record.generation_id, record);\n      accumulated.push(record);\n    },\n    records(): MaterializedInputRecord[] {\n      return [...accumulated];\n    },\n    cached(generationId: string): MaterializedInputRecord | null {\n      return byGenerationId.get(generationId) ?? null;\n    },\n  };\n}\n"
```json
}
```

# Local-only generations as worker task inputs

Read CLAUDE.md at the repo root first — it has cross-cutting rules and points to relevant sub-docs (especially `task_worker_lifecycle.md`, `unified_task_creation.md`, `storage_uploads.md`, `edge_functions.md`).

## Background

The app now supports `storage_mode='local'` generations (see `src/shared/lib/media/createGenerationFromFile.ts` → `createGenerationForLocalFile()`). The bytes live in the user's browser via a `FileSystemFileHandle` persisted in IndexedDB; the DB row carries `local_handle_id` instead of a `location` URL.

Today, when a user takes a generation and uses it as **input** to a worker task (travel, refine, masked-edit, etc.), the app puts a Supabase Storage URL into task params and the worker fetches it via HTTP. For local-only generations, that URL doesn't exist — and the worker has no way to reach into the browser.

This task wires those local-only generations through to the worker correctly, with a tiered strategy.

## Design

Implement a **per-input** resolution layer that runs at task-create time. For each input that references a generation:

1. If `storage_mode === 'remote'` (or absent / 'uploading' that has materialized) → use existing URL behavior. No change.
2. If `storage_mode === 'local'`:
   - **Detect whether a local worker is reachable** via a healthcheck (e.g. `GET http://localhost:<configured-port>/health` with a short timeout, ~250ms). Cache the answer for the duration of the task-creation call (don't re-probe per input).
   - **If local worker reachable**: read the file bytes from the FileSystemFileHandle, write them to a known shared dir (e.g. `~/.reigh-local-files/<local_handle_id>.<ext>`), and put a `file://` URL pointing at that path into the task params. The worker's `download_utils.py` already handles `file://` URLs (verify this — `reigh-worker/source/utils/download_utils.py` around line 60), so no worker changes should be needed. The materialized file is the "duplicate" per user wording.
   - **If no local worker**: upload the file bytes to Supabase Storage on demand. Reuse the existing upload helper in `src/shared/lib/media/imageUploader.ts`. Put the resulting public URL into task params. Mark the generation row with the new `location` (or a sibling `materialized_location`) so a second use of the same input doesn't re-upload — idempotent.

## Mixed inputs

A single task can reference both local-only and remote generations as inputs. The resolver MUST operate per-input, not per-task. After resolution, the task params contain a uniform set of URL strings (mix of `https://...` and `file://...`) — the worker doesn't know or care which inputs were originally local.

## Cleanup ("delete the duplicate after")

After task completion, the duplicate created during resolution must be cleaned up so we don't accumulate orphaned copies:

- **Local-worker `file://` materialization**: when the task completes, the file at `~/.reigh-local-files/<handle_id>.<ext>` is no longer needed. Delete it. Implement this in the `complete_task` edge function path OR via a worker-side cleanup hook OR via an app-side post-completion handler — whichever is most natural given the existing complete-task lifecycle. The original FileSystemFileHandle in the browser is untouched; we only delete the materialized copy.
- **Remote-worker upload-on-demand**: this is more nuanced. If we keep the uploaded copy, the generation effectively becomes remote-mode, defeating the user's local choice. Recommended: keep the upload only for the duration of the task (idempotency caching) and delete it after task completion. Update the generation row to remove the cached URL. Same lifecycle hook as above. If the user uses the same local generation as input again later, we re-upload (small cost, preserves intent).

The lifecycle hook should look at the resolved task params, identify which entries were materializations of local generations (mark them at creation time so cleanup knows), and clean each up. Don't touch generations that were natively remote.

## Detection of local worker

The localhost healthcheck endpoint and port: check existing reigh-worker server entrypoint (`reigh-worker/source/runtime/worker/server.py`) for the actual healthcheck route + port. If none exists, you'll need to add a tiny `/health` endpoint to the worker (returns 200 OK + JSON `{ok:true}`). Keep this minimal.

The app also needs to know which port to probe — read it from an env var (`VITE_LOCAL_WORKER_HEALTHCHECK_URL` or similar), default to a sensible value. Don't hard-code.

If the healthcheck fails (timeout, connection refused), fall back to remote behavior. Don't surface an error to the user — silent fallback is correct UX.

## Where to put the resolution layer

There's a unified task-creation path in `src/shared/lib/tasks/`. Look for the common entry point (probably a hook like `useCreateTask` or a shared `createTask` helper). The resolver should run there, immediately before the create-task edge function call. Sub-doc `unified_task_creation.md` is authoritative — read it first.

For tasks that build their own params (e.g. `src/shared/lib/tasks/travelBetweenImages/segmentImages.ts`, `src/shared/lib/tasks/imageEditing/buildMaskedEditTaskParams.ts`), the resolver needs a hook into each. Consider whether the resolver runs at the very end of param assembly (one place to plug in) or whether each task builder calls it explicitly. The first option is simpler and harder to forget.

## What NOT to do

- Do NOT make the worker do FileSystemFileHandle deserialization. Browser handles can't cross processes.
- Do NOT eagerly upload all local files at drop time. That defeats the point — only materialize on USE.
- Do NOT add a "this will be uploaded to cloud, OK?" prompt. The fallback should be silent. (We can add UX later if needed.)
- Do NOT refactor the unified task-creation system. Plug into it.
- Do NOT add comments explaining the change. The diff speaks for itself.

## Tests

- Add tests for the resolver covering: all-remote inputs (passthrough), all-local + local worker present (file:// path), all-local + remote only (upload + cache), mixed inputs (per-input branching), cleanup after completion.
- Mock the healthcheck and the upload helper. Don't hit real network.
- Mirror existing test patterns in `src/shared/lib/tasks/__tests__/` or wherever co-located tests live.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` — must not introduce new errors beyond pre-existing patterns.
- `npx vitest run` for affected directories.
- Manually trace through one task type (travel-between-images is a good one) to verify the resolver runs and the URL contract holds.

## Deliverables

- The per-input resolver, wired into the unified task-creation path.
- Local-worker healthcheck utility.
- Cleanup hook on task completion.
- A `/health` endpoint on the worker if one doesn't exist.
- Tests covering the matrix above.

```
60	  const controller = new AbortController();
61	  const handleAbort = () => controller.abort();
62	  if (signal?.aborted) {
63	    controller.abort();
64	  }
65	  signal?.addEventListener('abort', handleAbort);
66	  const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeoutMs);
67	  try {
68	    return await fetch(url, {
69	      method: 'POST',
70	      headers,
71	      body,
72	      signal: controller.signal,
73	    });
74	  } finally {
75	    clearTimeout(timeout);
76	    signal?.removeEventListener('abort', handleAbort);
77	  }
78	}

80	function addGenerationId(target: Set<string>, value: unknown): void {
81	  if (typeof value !== 'string') {
82	    return;
83	  }
84	
85	  const trimmed = value.trim();
86	  if (trimmed) {
87	    target.add(trimmed);
88	  }
89	}
90	
91	function addGenerationIdsFromArray(target: Set<string>, value: unknown): void {
92	  if (!Array.isArray(value)) {
93	    return;
94	  }
95	
96	  value.forEach((item) => addGenerationId(target, item));
97	}

99	function collectGenerationIds(value: unknown, target: Set<string>): void {
100	  if (!value) {
101	    return;
102	  }
103	
104	  if (Array.isArray(value)) {
105	    value.forEach((item) => collectGenerationIds(item, target));
106	    return;
107	  }
108	
109	  if (typeof value !== 'object') {
110	    return;
111	  }
112	
113	  const record = value as Record<string, unknown>;
114	  for (const [key, nestedValue] of Object.entries(record)) {
115	    if (DIRECT_GENERATION_ID_KEYS.has(key)) {
116	      addGenerationId(target, nestedValue);
117	      continue;
118	    }
119	
120	    if (ARRAY_GENERATION_ID_KEYS.has(key)) {
121	      addGenerationIdsFromArray(target, nestedValue);
122	      continue;
123	    }
124	
125	    collectGenerationIds(nestedValue, target);
126	  }
127	}

129	async function materializeTaskInputGenerations(
130	  input: Record<string, unknown>,
131	  options?: CreateTaskOptions,
132	): Promise<void> {

134	  collectGenerationIds(input, generationIds);

136	  if (generationIds.size === 0) {

167	 * Creates a task using the unified create-task edge function.
168	 * Retries once on timeout since the server typically responds in <2s.
169	 */
170	export async function createTask(
171	  taskParams: BaseTaskParams,
172	  options?: CreateTaskOptions,
173	): Promise<TaskCreationResult> {
174	  const [REDACTED]();
175	
176	  if (!accessToken) {
177	    throw new AuthError('Please log in to create tasks', { needsLogin: true });
178	  }
179	
180	  const startTime = Date.now();
181	  const requestId = `${startTime}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}`;
182	  const taskIdentifier = taskParams.family;
183	  const requestContext = {
184	    requestId,
185	    taskType: taskIdentifier,
186	    projectId: taskParams.project_id,
187	  };
188	
189	  // Idempotency key stays the same across retries so the server
190	  // deduplicates if the first attempt actually landed.
191	  const idempotency_key = generateUUID();
192	  const url = `${getSupabaseUrl()}/functions/v1/create-task`;
193	  await materializeTaskInputGenerations(taskParams.input, options);
194	  const headers = {
195	    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
196	    Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
197	    [REDACTED](),
198	  };
199	  const body = JSON.stringify({
200	    family: taskParams.family,
201	    project_id: taskParams.project_id,
202	    input: taskParams.input,
203	    idempotency_key,
204	  });
205	
206	  let lastError: unknown;
207	
208	  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= MAX_ATTEMPTS; attempt++) {
209	    try {
210	      const response = await attemptCreateTask(url, headers, body, ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS, options?.signal);
211	
212	      if (!response.ok) {
213	        const errorText = await response.text().catch(() => '');
214	        throw new ServerError(errorText || 'Failed to create task', {
215	          context: requestContext,
216	        });
217	      }
218	
219	      const data = await response.json() as unknown;
220	      return parseTaskCreationResponse(data, requestContext);
221	    } catch (err: unknown) {
222	      lastError = err;
223	      const durationMs = Date.now() - startTime;
224	      const isTimeout = isAbortError(err);
225	
226	      if (isTimeout && attempt < MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
227	        console.error('[createTask] attempt %d/%d timed out after %dms, retrying', attempt, MAX_ATTEMPTS, durationMs, {
228	          ...requestContext,
229	          network: getNetworkDiagnostics(),
230	        });
231	        continue;
232	      }
233	
234	      const context = {
235	        ...requestContext,
236	        attempt,
237	        durationMs,
238	        network: getNetworkDiagnostics(),
239	        errorType: err instanceof Error ? err.name : typeof err,
240	        errorMessage: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err),
241	      };
242	
243	      console.error('[createTask] FAILED after %d attempt(s), %dms', attempt, durationMs, context);
244	
245	      if (isTimeout) {
246	        throw new NetworkError('Task creation timed out. Please try again.', {
247	          isTimeout: true,
248	          context,
249	          cause: err instanceof Error ? err : undefined,
250	        });
251	      }
252	
253	      normalizeAndPresentAndRethrow(err, {
254	        context: 'TaskCreation',
255	        showToast: false,
256	        logData: context,
257	      });
258	    }
259	  }
260	
261	  // Unreachable, but TypeScript needs it
262	  throw lastError;
263	}
```

```
268	export async function materializeLocalGeneration(
269	  generationId: string,
270	  options?: MaterializeLocalGenerationOptions,
271	): Promise<{ location: string }> {
272	  const existingPromise = inFlightMaterializations.get(generationId);
273	  if (existingPromise) {
274	    return existingPromise;
275	  }
276	
277	  const promise = materializeLocalGenerationInternal(generationId, options).finally(() => {
278	    inFlightMaterializations.delete(generationId);
279	  });
280	
281	  inFlightMaterializations.set(generationId, promise);
```

```
94	  const { file, filePath, accessToken, timeoutMs, signal, onProgress } = input;

98	    const xhr = new XMLHttpRequest();
99	    const lifecycle = createUploadXhrLifecycle();
100	
101	    const fail = (error: Error) => {
102	      lifecycle.cleanup();
103	      signal?.removeEventListener('abort', abortHandler);
104	      reject(error);
105	    };
106	
107	    const abortHandler = () => {
108	      xhr.abort();
109	      fail(new Error('Upload cancelled'));
110	    };
111	
112	    lifecycle.overallTimeout = setTimeout(() => {
113	      xhr.abort();
114	      fail(new Error(`Upload timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms`));

118	      const timeSinceLastProgress = lifecycle.millisecondsSinceProgress();

129	      lifecycle.cleanup();

132	        onProgress?.(100);

195	  const { maxRetries, onProgress: progressCallback, signal, timeoutMs } = options;
196	
197	  if (!file) {
198	    throw new Error('No file provided');
199	  }
200	
201	  if (signal?.aborted) {
202	    throw new Error('Upload cancelled');
203	  }
204	
205	  const userId = await requireSessionUserId();
206	  const fileExtension = getFileExtension(file.name, file.type);
207	  const filename = generateUniqueFilename(fileExtension);
208	  const filePath = storagePaths.upload(userId, filename);
209	  const fileSizeMB = (file.size / (1024 * 1024)).toFixed(2);
210	
211	  let lastError: unknown;
212	
213	  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++) {
214	    if (signal?.aborted) {
215	      throw new Error('Upload cancelled');
216	    }
217	
218	    try {
219	      const accessToken = await requireAccessToken();
220	      await uploadFileWithXhr({

222	        filePath,
223	        accessToken,
224	        timeoutMs,
225	        signal,
226	        onProgress: progressCallback,
227	      });

230	    } catch (error) {
231	      lastError = error;
232	      const errorMsg = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
233

237	      if (isCancelledError(errorMsg)) {
238	        throw error;
239	      }
240	
241	      if (attempt < maxRetries) {
242	        await wait(getRetryDelay(attempt));
243	      }
244	    }
245	  }
246	
247	  normalizeAndPresentError(lastError, { context: `ImageUpload:allRetriesFailed:${file.name}`, showToast: false });
```

```
135	      }
136	    }, 10000);

138	    options.signal?.addEventListener('abort', abortHandler);
139	    attachUploadProgressListener(xhr, options.onProgress, lifecycle.markProgress);

144	      if (xhr.status >= 200 && xhr.status < 300) {
```

```
18	    return configuredBase;
```

```
16	 * Get the canonical generation ID from a media item.
17	 * Handles both direct generations (id) and variants (generation_id).
18	 * Also checks metadata.generation_id for compatibility with various data shapes.
19	 *
20	 * Priority: generation_id > metadata.generation_id > id
21	 *
22	 * @example
23	 * // Instead of: (media as unknown).generation_id || media.id
24	 * const genId = getGenerationId(media);
25	 */
26	export function getGenerationId(
27	  media: MaybeHasGenerationId | null | undefined
28	): string | null {
29	  if (!media) return null;
30	  const metadataGenerationId = typeof media.metadata?.generation_id === 'string'
31	    ? media.metadata.generation_id
32	    : null;
33	  return media.generation_id || metadataGenerationId || media.id || null;
34	}
35	
36	/**
37	 * Centralized preload eligibility contract for URL-based media entries.
38	 */
39	export function isPreloadableMediaUrl(url: string | null | undefined): boolean {
40	  if (!url) {
41	    return false;
42	  }
43	
44	  return !NON_PRELOADABLE_URL_MARKERS.some((marker) => url.includes(marker));
45	}
46	
47	/**
48	 * Media item with various URL properties (normalized across sources)
49	 */
50	interface MediaWithUrls {
51	  location?: string | null;
52	  url?: string | null;
53	  thumbnail_url?: string | null;
54	  thumbUrl?: string | null;
55	  imageUrl?: string | null;
56	}
57	
58	function getFirstNonEmptyUrl(...urls: Array<string | null | undefined>): string | undefined {
59	  for (const url of urls) {
60	    if (typeof url !== 'string') {
61	      continue;
62	    }
63	
64	    const trimmed = url.trim();
65	    if (trimmed.length > 0) {
66	      return trimmed;
67	    }
68	  }
69	
70	  return undefined;
71	}
72	
73	export function getMediaUrl(media: MediaWithUrls | null | undefined): string | undefined {
74	  if (!media) return undefined;
75	  return getFirstNonEmptyUrl(media.location, media.url, media.imageUrl);
76	}
77	
78	export function getThumbnailUrl(media: MediaWithUrls | null | undefined): string | undefined {
79	  if (!media) return undefined;
80	  return getFirstNonEmptyUrl(media.thumbnail_url, media.thumbUrl);
81	}
82	
83	/** Transform a variant to a GenerationRow shape for lightbox display. */
84	export function variantToGenerationRow(
85	  media: {
86	    id: string;
87	    url: string;
88	    thumbUrl?: string;
89	    createdAt?: string;
90	    starred?: boolean;
91	    metadata?: { prompt?: string; tool_type?: string; variant_type?: string; generation_id?: string | null };
92	    generation_id?: string | null;
93	  },
94	  mediaType: 'video' | 'image',
95	): GenerationRow {
96	  const generationId = getGenerationId(media) ?? media.id;
97	
98	  return {
99	    id: media.id,
100	    generation_id: generationId,
101	    location: media.url,
102	    thumbUrl: media.thumbUrl,
103	    type: mediaType,
104	    createdAt: media.createdAt,

108	      variant_type: media.metadata?.variant_type,
109	      variant_id: media.id,
110	    },
111	    starred: media.starred ?? false,
112	  };
113	}
```

```
import type { GenerationRow } from '@/domains/generation/types';
import type { Database } from '@/integrations/supabase/databasePublicTypes';
import { coerceGenerationRowDto, mapGenerationRowDtoToRow } from '@/domains/generation/mappers/generationRowMapper';
import { getSupabaseClient as supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
import {
  createRepositoryQueryError,
  createInvalidRowShapeError,
  isRepositoryNoRowsError,
} from './repositoryErrors';

type GenerationRecord = Database['public']['Tables']['generations']['Row'] & Record<string, unknown>;

export async function fetchGenerationById(generationId: string): Promise<GenerationRow | null> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase().from('generations')
    .select('*')
    .eq('id', generationId)
    .maybeSingle();

  if (error) {
    if (isRepositoryNoRowsError(error)) {
      return null;
    }
    throw createRepositoryQueryError('generation', error, { generationId });
  }

  if (!data) {
    return null;
  }

  const row = coerceGenerationRowDto(data);
  if (!row) {
    throw createInvalidRowShapeError('generation', { generationId });
  }

  return mapGenerationRowDtoToRow(row);
}

export async function fetchGenerationRecordById(generationId: string): Promise<GenerationRecord | null> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase().from('generations')
    .select('*')
    .eq('id', generationId)
    .maybeSingle();

  if (error) {
    if (isRepositoryNoRowsError(error)) {
      return null;
    }
    throw createRepositoryQueryError('generation record', error, { generationId });
  }

  if (!data) {
    return null;
  }

  return data as GenerationRecord;
}
```

```
19	function getNetworkDiagnostics(): Record<string, unknown> {
20	  const diag: Record<string, unknown> = {
21	    online: navigator.onLine,
22	  };
23	  const conn = (navigator as Navigator & { connection?: { effectiveType?: string; downlink?: number; rtt?: number } }).connection;
24	  if (conn) {
25	    diag.effectiveType = conn.effectiveType;
26	    diag.downlink = conn.downlink;
27	    diag.rtt = conn.rtt;
28	  }
29	  return diag;
30	}

32	async function attemptCreateTask(
33	  url: string,
34	  headers: Record<string, string>,
35	  body: string,
36	  timeoutMs: number,
37	  signal?: AbortSignal,
38	): Promise<Response> {
39	  const controller = new AbortController();
40	  const handleAbort = () => controller.abort();
41	  if (signal?.aborted) {
42	    controller.abort();
43	  }
44	  signal?.addEventListener('abort', handleAbort);
45	  const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeoutMs);
46	  try {
47	    return await fetch(url, {
48	      method: 'POST',
49	      headers,
50	      body,
51	      signal: controller.signal,
52	    });
53	  } finally {
54	    clearTimeout(timeout);
55	    signal?.removeEventListener('abort', handleAbort);
56	  }
57	}
58	
59	/**
60	 * Creates a task using the unified create-task edge function.
61	 * Retries once on timeout since the server typically responds in <2s.
62	 */
63	export async function createTask(
64	  taskParams: BaseTaskParams,
65	  options?: CreateTaskOptions,
66	): Promise<TaskCreationResult> {
67	  const [REDACTED]();
68	
69	  if (!accessToken) {
70	    throw new AuthError('Please log in to create tasks', { needsLogin: true });
71	  }
72	
73	  const startTime = Date.now();
74	  const requestId = `${startTime}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}`;
75	  const taskIdentifier = taskParams.family;
76	  const requestContext = {
77	    requestId,
78	    taskType: taskIdentifier,
79	    projectId: taskParams.project_id,
80	  };
81	
82	  // Idempotency key stays the same across retries so the server
83	  // deduplicates if the first attempt actually landed.
84	  const idempotency_key = generateUUID();
85	  const url = `${getSupabaseUrl()}/functions/v1/create-task`;
86	  const materializations = options?.localWorkerSession?.records() ?? [];
87	  const headers = {
88	    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
89	    Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
90	    [REDACTED](),
91	  };
92	  const body = JSON.stringify({
93	    family: taskParams.family,
94	    project_id: taskParams.project_id,
95	    input: taskParams.input,
96	    idempotency_key,
97	    ...(materializations.length > 0 ? { materialized_inputs: materializations } : {}),
98	  });
99	
100	  let lastError: unknown;
101	
102	  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= MAX_ATTEMPTS; attempt++) {
103	    try {
104	      const response = await attemptCreateTask(url, headers, body, ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS, options?.signal);
105	
106	      if (!response.ok) {
107	        const errorText = await response.text().catch(() => '');
108	        throw new ServerError(errorText || 'Failed to create task', {
109	          context: requestContext,
110	        });
111	      }
112	
113	      const data = await response.json() as unknown;
114	      return parseTaskCreationResponse(data, requestContext);
115	    } catch (err: unknown) {
116	      lastError = err;
117	      const durationMs = Date.now() - startTime;
118	      const isTimeout = isAbortError(err);
119	
120	      if (isTimeout && attempt < MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
121	        console.error('[createTask] attempt %d/%d timed out after %dms, retrying', attempt, MAX_ATTEMPTS, durationMs, {
122	          ...requestContext,
123	          network: getNetworkDiagnostics(),
124	        });
125	        continue;
126	      }
127	
128	      const context = {
129	        ...requestContext,
130	        attempt,
131	        durationMs,
132	        network: getNetworkDiagnostics(),
133	        errorType: err instanceof Error ? err.name : typeof err,
134	        errorMessage: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err),
135	      };
136	
137	      console.error('[createTask] FAILED after %d attempt(s), %dms', attempt, durationMs, context);
138	
139	      if (isTimeout) {
140	        throw new NetworkError('Task creation timed out. Please try again.', {
141	          isTimeout: true,
142	          context,
143	          cause: err instanceof Error ? err : undefined,
144	        });
145	      }
146	
147	      normalizeAndPresentAndRethrow(err, {
148	        context: 'TaskCreation',
149	        showToast: false,
150	        logData: context,
151	      });
152	    }
153	  }
154	
155	  // Unreachable, but TypeScript needs it
156	  throw lastError;
157	}
```

# Local-only generations as worker task inputs

Read CLAUDE.md at the repo root first — it has cross-cutting rules and points to relevant sub-docs (especially `task_worker_lifecycle.md`, `unified_task_creation.md`, `storage_uploads.md`, `edge_functions.md`).

## Background

The app now supports `storage_mode='local'` generations (see `src/shared/lib/media/createGenerationFromFile.ts` → `createGenerationForLocalFile()`). The bytes live in the user's browser via a `FileSystemFileHandle` persisted in IndexedDB; the DB row carries `local_handle_id` instead of a `location` URL.

Today, when a user takes a generation and uses it as **input** to a worker task (travel, refine, masked-edit, etc.), the app puts a Supabase Storage URL into task params and the worker fetches it via HTTP. For local-only generations, that URL doesn't exist — and the worker has no way to reach into the browser.

This task wires those local-only generations through to the worker correctly, with a tiered strategy.

## Design

Implement a **per-input** resolution layer that runs at task-create time. For each input that references a generation:

1. If `storage_mode === 'remote'` (or absent / 'uploading' that has materialized) → use existing URL behavior. No change.
2. If `storage_mode === 'local'`:
   - **Detect whether a local worker is reachable** via a healthcheck (e.g. `GET http://localhost:<configured-port>/health` with a short timeout, ~250ms). Cache the answer for the duration of the task-creation call (don't re-probe per input).
   - **If local worker reachable**: read the file bytes from the FileSystemFileHandle, write them to a known shared dir (e.g. `~/.reigh-local-files/<local_handle_id>.<ext>`), and put a `file://` URL pointing at that path into the task params. The worker's `download_utils.py` already handles `file://` URLs (verify this — `reigh-worker/source/utils/download_utils.py` around line 60), so no worker changes should be needed. The materialized file is the "duplicate" per user wording.
   - **If no local worker**: upload the file bytes to Supabase Storage on demand. Reuse the existing upload helper in `src/shared/lib/media/imageUploader.ts`. Put the resulting public URL into task params. Mark the generation row with the new `location` (or a sibling `materialized_location`) so a second use of the same input doesn't re-upload — idempotent.

## Mixed inputs

A single task can reference both local-only and remote generations as inputs. The resolver MUST operate per-input, not per-task. After resolution, the task params contain a uniform set of URL strings (mix of `https://...` and `file://...`) — the worker doesn't know or care which inputs were originally local.

## Cleanup ("delete the duplicate after")

After task completion, the duplicate created during resolution must be cleaned up so we don't accumulate orphaned copies:

- **Local-worker `file://` materialization**: when the task completes, the file at `~/.reigh-local-files/<handle_id>.<ext>` is no longer needed. Delete it. Implement this in the `complete_task` edge function path OR via a worker-side cleanup hook OR via an app-side post-completion handler — whichever is most natural given the existing complete-task lifecycle. The original FileSystemFileHandle in the browser is untouched; we only delete the materialized copy.
- **Remote-worker upload-on-demand**: this is more nuanced. If we keep the uploaded copy, the generation effectively becomes remote-mode, defeating the user's local choice. Recommended: keep the upload only for the duration of the task (idempotency caching) and delete it after task completion. Update the generation row to remove the cached URL. Same lifecycle hook as above. If the user uses the same local generation as input again later, we re-upload (small cost, preserves intent).

The lifecycle hook should look at the resolved task params, identify which entries were materializations of local generations (mark them at creation time so cleanup knows), and clean each up. Don't touch generations that were natively remote.

## Detection of local worker

The localhost healthcheck endpoint and port: check existing reigh-worker server entrypoint (`reigh-worker/source/runtime/worker/server.py`) for the actual healthcheck route + port. If none exists, you'll need to add a tiny `/health` endpoint to the worker (returns 200 OK + JSON `{ok:true}`). Keep this minimal.

The app also needs to know which port to probe — read it from an env var (`VITE_LOCAL_WORKER_HEALTHCHECK_URL` or similar), default to a sensible value. Don't hard-code.

If the healthcheck fails (timeout, connection refused), fall back to remote behavior. Don't surface an error to the user — silent fallback is correct UX.

## Where to put the resolution layer

There's a unified task-creation path in `src/shared/lib/tasks/`. Look for the common entry point (probably a hook like `useCreateTask` or a shared `createTask` helper). The resolver should run there, immediately before the create-task edge function call. Sub-doc `unified_task_creation.md` is authoritative — read it first.

For tasks that build their own params (e.g. `src/shared/lib/tasks/travelBetweenImages/segmentImages.ts`, `src/shared/lib/tasks/imageEditing/buildMaskedEditTaskParams.ts`), the resolver needs a hook into each. Consider whether the resolver runs at the very end of param assembly (one place to plug in) or whether each task builder calls it explicitly. The first option is simpler and harder to forget.

## What NOT to do

- Do NOT make the worker do FileSystemFileHandle deserialization. Browser handles can't cross processes.
- Do NOT eagerly upload all local files at drop time. That defeats the point — only materialize on USE.
- Do NOT add a "this will be uploaded to cloud, OK?" prompt. The fallback should be silent. (We can add UX later if needed.)
- Do NOT refactor the unified task-creation system. Plug into it.
- Do NOT add comments explaining the change. The diff speaks for itself.

## Tests

- Add tests for the resolver covering: all-remote inputs (passthrough), all-local + local worker present (file:// path), all-local + remote only (upload + cache), mixed inputs (per-input branching), cleanup after completion.
- Mock the healthcheck and the upload helper. Don't hit real network.
- Mirror existing test patterns in `src/shared/lib/tasks/__tests__/` or wherever co-located tests live.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` — must not introduce new errors beyond pre-existing patterns.
- `npx vitest run` for affected directories.
- Manually trace through one task type (travel-between-images is a good one) to verify the resolver runs and the URL contract holds.

## Deliverables

- The per-input resolver, wired into the unified task-creation path.
- Local-worker healthcheck utility.
- Cleanup hook on task completion.
- A `/health` endpoint on the worker if one doesn't exist.
- Tests covering the matrix above.

```
397	    projectAspectRatio = typeof projectData?.aspect_ratio === "string"
398	      ? projectData.aspect_ratio
399	      : null;
400	  }
401	
402	  if (projectAspectRatio === null) {
403	    const { data: projectData, error: projectError } = await supabaseAdmin
404	      .from("projects")
405	      .select("aspect_ratio")
406	      .eq("id", finalProjectId)
407	      .single();
408	
409	    if (projectError) {
410	      logger.error("Project aspect ratio lookup error", {
411	        project_id: finalProjectId,
412	        error: projectError.message,
413	      });
414	      await logger.flush();
415	      return createErrorResponse("Project not found", 404, "project_not_found", false);
416	    }
417	
418	    projectAspectRatio = typeof projectData?.aspect_ratio === "string"
419	      ? projectData.aspect_ratio
420	      : null;
421	  }
422	
423	  try {
424	    let resolver = getTaskFamilyResolver(resolverRequest.family);
425	    if (!resolver) {
426	      // No explicit resolver — check if this task type exists in the DB.
427	      // Worker-created child tasks (category: "processing") don't need
428	      // validation, just a passthrough insert.
429	      const { data: taskType } = await supabaseAdmin
430	        .from("task_types")
431	        .select("name")
432	        .eq("name", resolverRequest.family)
433	        .eq("is_active", true)
434	        .maybeSingle();
435	
436	      if (!taskType) {
437	        logger.error("Unknown task family", { family: resolverRequest.family });
438	        await logger.flush();
439	        return createErrorResponse("Unknown task family", 400, "unknown_task_family", false);
440	      }
441	
442	      resolver = createWorkerPassthroughResolver(resolverRequest.family);
443	    }
444	
445	    const resolverResult = await resolver(resolverRequest, {
446	      supabaseAdmin,
447	      projectId: finalProjectId,
448	      aspectRatio: projectAspectRatio,
449	      logger,
450	    });
451	
452	    if (!Array.isArray(resolverResult.tasks) || resolverResult.tasks.length === 0) {
453	      logger.error("Resolver returned no tasks", { family: resolverRequest.family });
454	      await logger.flush();
455	      return createErrorResponse("Resolver did not return any tasks", 500, "invalid_resolver_result");
456	    }
457	
458	    const insertObjects = resolverResult.tasks;
459	    const responseMeta = resolverResult.meta;
460	
461	    const createdTaskIds: string[] = [];
462	    let deduplicatedCount = 0;
463	
464	    for (let taskIndex = 0; taskIndex < insertObjects.length; taskIndex++) {
465	      const insertObject = insertObjects[taskIndex];
466	      const idempotencyKey = await resolveInsertIdempotencyKey(
467	        insertObject,
468	        requestIdempotencyKey,
469	        taskIndex,
470	        insertObjects.length,
471	      );
472	
473	      const insertResult = await insertTaskWithRecovery({
474	        supabaseAdmin,
475	        insertObject,
476	        idempotencyKey,
477	        finalProjectId,
478	        isServiceRole,
479	        logger,
480	      });
481	
482	      if (!insertResult.ok) {
483	        return insertResult.response;
484	      }
485	
486	      createdTaskIds.push(insertResult.taskId);
487	      if (insertResult.deduplicated) {
488	        deduplicatedCount += 1;
489	      }
490	    }
491	
492	    if (createdTaskIds.length === 1) {
493	      logger.setDefaultTaskId(createdTaskIds[0]);
494	    }
495	
496	    logger.info("Task created successfully", {
497	      task_id: createdTaskIds[0],
498	      task_ids: insertObjects.length > 1 ? createdTaskIds : undefined,
499	      task_count: createdTaskIds.length,
500	      task_family: resolverRequest.family,
501	      project_id: finalProjectId,
502	      created_by: isServiceRole ? "service-role" : callerId,
503	      has_idempotency_key: !!requestIdempotencyKey,
504	      deduplicated_count: deduplicatedCount,
505	    });
506	
507	    await logger.flush();
508	    return buildCreateTaskResponse(createdTaskIds, {
509	      meta: responseMeta,
510	      deduplicated: createdTaskIds.length === 1 && deduplicatedCount === 1,
511	    });
512	  } catch (error: unknown) {
513	    if (error instanceof TaskValidationError) {
514	      logger.error("Validation error", { error: error.message, field: error.field });
515	      await logger.flush();
516	      return createErrorResponse(error.message, 400, "validation_error", false);
517	    }
518	
519	    const message = getErrorMessage(error);
520	    logger.critical("Unexpected error", { error: message });
521	    await logger.flush();
522	    return createErrorResponse("Internal server error", 500, "internal_server_error");
523	  }
524	});
525
```

```json
  "new_string": "function parseRequestIdempotencyKey(body: unknown): string | undefined {\n  if (!isRecord(body)) {\n    return undefined;\n  }\n\n  return asNonEmptyString(body.idempotency_key) ?? undefined;\n}\n\nfunction parseMaterializedInputs(\n  body: unknown,\n): { ok: true; value: MaterializedInputRecord[] | undefined } | { ok: false; error: string } {\n  if (!isRecord(body) || !(\"materialized_inputs\" in body) || body.materialized_inputs == null) {\n    return { ok: true, value: undefined };\n  }\n\n  const raw = body.materialized_inputs;\n  if (!Array.isArray(raw)) {\n    return { ok: false, error: \"materialized_inputs must be an array when provided\" };\n  }\n\n  const result: MaterializedInputRecord[] = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < raw.length; i++) {\n    const entry = raw[i];\n    if (!isRecord(entry)) {\n      return { ok: false, error: `materialized_inputs[${i}] must be an object` };\n    }\n    const generationId = asNonEmptyString(entry.generation_id);\n    const target = asNonEmptyString(entry.target);\n    const kind = entry.kind;\n    if (!generationId) {\n      return { ok: false, error: `materialized_inputs[${i}].generation_id must be a non-empty string` };\n    }\n    if (kind !== \"file\" && kind !== \"remote\") {\n      return { ok: false, error: `materialized_inputs[${i}].kind must be 'file' or 'remote'` };\n    }\n    if (!target) {\n      return { ok: false, error: `materialized_inputs[${i}].target must be a non-empty string` };\n    }\n    result.push({ generation_id: generationId, kind, target });\n  }\n\n  return { ok: true, value: result.length > 0 ? result : undefined };\n}"
}
```

# Local-only generations as worker task inputs

Read CLAUDE.md at the repo root first — it has cross-cutting rules and points to relevant sub-docs (especially `task_worker_lifecycle.md`, `unified_task_creation.md`, `storage_uploads.md`, `edge_functions.md`).

## Background

The app now supports `storage_mode='local'` generations (see `src/shared/lib/media/createGenerationFromFile.ts` → `createGenerationForLocalFile()`). The bytes live in the user's browser via a `FileSystemFileHandle` persisted in IndexedDB; the DB row carries `local_handle_id` instead of a `location` URL.

Today, when a user takes a generation and uses it as **input** to a worker task (travel, refine, masked-edit, etc.), the app puts a Supabase Storage URL into task params and the worker fetches it via HTTP. For local-only generations, that URL doesn't exist — and the worker has no way to reach into the browser.

This task wires those local-only generations through to the worker correctly, with a tiered strategy.

## Design

Implement a **per-input** resolution layer that runs at task-create time. For each input that references a generation:

1. If `storage_mode === 'remote'` (or absent / 'uploading' that has materialized) → use existing URL behavior. No change.
2. If `storage_mode === 'local'`:
   - **Detect whether a local worker is reachable** via a healthcheck (e.g. `GET http://localhost:<configured-port>/health` with a short timeout, ~250ms). Cache the answer for the duration of the task-creation call (don't re-probe per input).
   - **If local worker reachable**: read the file bytes from the FileSystemFileHandle, write them to a known shared dir (e.g. `~/.reigh-local-files/<local_handle_id>.<ext>`), and put a `file://` URL pointing at that path into the task params. The worker's `download_utils.py` already handles `file://` URLs (verify this — `reigh-worker/source/utils/download_utils.py` around line 60), so no worker changes should be needed. The materialized file is the "duplicate" per user wording.
   - **If no local worker**: upload the file bytes to Supabase Storage on demand. Reuse the existing upload helper in `src/shared/lib/media/imageUploader.ts`. Put the resulting public URL into task params. Mark the generation row with the new `location` (or a sibling `materialized_location`) so a second use of the same input doesn't re-upload — idempotent.

## Mixed inputs

A single task can reference both local-only and remote generations as inputs. The resolver MUST operate per-input, not per-task. After resolution, the task params contain a uniform set of URL strings (mix of `https://...` and `file://...`) — the worker doesn't know or care which inputs were originally local.

## Cleanup ("delete the duplicate after")

After task completion, the duplicate created during resolution must be cleaned up so we don't accumulate orphaned copies:

- **Local-worker `file://` materialization**: when the task completes, the file at `~/.reigh-local-files/<handle_id>.<ext>` is no longer needed. Delete it. Implement this in the `complete_task` edge function path OR via a worker-side cleanup hook OR via an app-side post-completion handler — whichever is most natural given the existing complete-task lifecycle. The original FileSystemFileHandle in the browser is untouched; we only delete the materialized copy.
- **Remote-worker upload-on-demand**: this is more nuanced. If we keep the uploaded copy, the generation effectively becomes remote-mode, defeating the user's local choice. Recommended: keep the upload only for the duration of the task (idempotency caching) and delete it after task completion. Update the generation row to remove the cached URL. Same lifecycle hook as above. If the user uses the same local generation as input again later, we re-upload (small cost, preserves intent).

The lifecycle hook should look at the resolved task params, identify which entries were materializations of local generations (mark them at creation time so cleanup knows), and clean each up. Don't touch generations that were natively remote.

## Detection of local worker

The localhost healthcheck endpoint and port: check existing reigh-worker server entrypoint (`reigh-worker/source/runtime/worker/server.py`) for the actual healthcheck route + port. If none exists, you'll need to add a tiny `/health` endpoint to the worker (returns 200 OK + JSON `{ok:true}`). Keep this minimal.

The app also needs to know which port to probe — read it from an env var (`VITE_LOCAL_WORKER_HEALTHCHECK_URL` or similar), default to a sensible value. Don't hard-code.

If the healthcheck fails (timeout, connection refused), fall back to remote behavior. Don't surface an error to the user — silent fallback is correct UX.

## Where to put the resolution layer

There's a unified task-creation path in `src/shared/lib/tasks/`. Look for the common entry point (probably a hook like `useCreateTask` or a shared `createTask` helper). The resolver should run there, immediately before the create-task edge function call. Sub-doc `unified_task_creation.md` is authoritative — read it first.

For tasks that build their own params (e.g. `src/shared/lib/tasks/travelBetweenImages/segmentImages.ts`, `src/shared/lib/tasks/imageEditing/buildMaskedEditTaskParams.ts`), the resolver needs a hook into each. Consider whether the resolver runs at the very end of param assembly (one place to plug in) or whether each task builder calls it explicitly. The first option is simpler and harder to forget.

## What NOT to do

- Do NOT make the worker do FileSystemFileHandle deserialization. Browser handles can't cross processes.
- Do NOT eagerly upload all local files at drop time. That defeats the point — only materialize on USE.
- Do NOT add a "this will be uploaded to cloud, OK?" prompt. The fallback should be silent. (We can add UX later if needed.)
- Do NOT refactor the unified task-creation system. Plug into it.
- Do NOT add comments explaining the change. The diff speaks for itself.

## Tests

- Add tests for the resolver covering: all-remote inputs (passthrough), all-local + local worker present (file:// path), all-local + remote only (upload + cache), mixed inputs (per-input branching), cleanup after completion.
- Mock the healthcheck and the upload helper. Don't hit real network.
- Mirror existing test patterns in `src/shared/lib/tasks/__tests__/` or wherever co-located tests live.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` — must not introduce new errors beyond pre-existing patterns.
- `npx vitest run` for affected directories.
- Manually trace through one task type (travel-between-images is a good one) to verify the resolver runs and the URL contract holds.

## Deliverables

- The per-input resolver, wired into the unified task-creation path.
- Local-worker healthcheck utility.
- Cleanup hook on task completion.
- A `/health` endpoint on the worker if one doesn't exist.
- Tests covering the matrix above.
- Brief summary in your final message: every task type touched, every caller of the create-task path you verified.

```
69	export async function createInpaintingTaskWorkflow({
70	  taskType,
71	  media,
72	  selectedProjectId,
73	  shotId,
74	  toolTypeOverride,
75	  loras,

94	  const maskFile = new File(

96	    `${config.fileNamePrefix}_${media.id}_${Date.now()}.png`,
97	    { type: 'image/png' },
98	  );
99	  const maskUrl = await uploadImageToStorage(maskFile);
100	
101	  const mediaUrl = getMediaUrl(media) || media.imageUrl;
102	  const sourceUrl = activeVariantLocation || mediaUrl;
103	  if (!sourceUrl) {
104	    throw new Error('Missing source media URL');
105	  }
106	
107	  return config.createTask(
108	    buildMaskedEditTaskParams({
109	      projectId: selectedProjectId,

111	      maskUrl,
112	      prompt: inpaintPrompt,
113	      numGenerations: inpaintNumGenerations,

121	      qwenEditModel,
122	    }),
```
