192	function buildSubmitParamsBuilder(
193	  effectiveSettings: SegmentSettings,
194	  task: SegmentTaskContext,
195	  images: SegmentTaskImageContext,
196	): BuildTaskParams {
197	  const selectedModel = effectiveSettings.selectedModel
198	    ?? resolveSelectedModelFromModelName(task.modelName);
199	  const spec = getModelSpec(selectedModel);
200	  const policy = resolveGenerationPolicy(spec, {
201	    smoothContinuations: effectiveSettings.smoothContinuations ?? false,
202	    requestedExecutionMode: task.generationTypeMode ?? 'i2v',
203	    guidanceKind: (() => {
204	      const guidance = task.structureInput?.travelGuidance;
205	      if (!guidance || guidance.kind === 'none') {
206	        return effectiveSettings.guidanceMode;
207	      }
208	      if (guidance.kind === 'uni3c') {
209	        return 'uni3c';
210	      }
211	      return guidance.mode;
212	    })(),
213	  });
214	  const continuationEnabled = task.segmentIndex > 0
215	    && policy.continuation.enabled
216	    && policy.continuation.strategy !== undefined;
217	
218	  return (prompt: string, enhancedPromptParam?: string) => {
219	    return buildTaskParams(
220	      { ...effectiveSettings, prompt },
221	      {
222	        projectId: task.projectId,
223	        shotId: task.shotId,
224	        generationId: task.generationId,
225	        childGenerationId: task.childGenerationId,
226	        segmentIndex: task.segmentIndex,
227	        startImageUrl: images.startImageUrl ?? '',
228	        endImageUrl: images.endImageUrl,
229	        startImageGenerationId: images.startImageGenerationId,
230	        endImageGenerationId: images.endImageGenerationId,
231	        startImageVariantId: images.startImageVariantId,
232	        endImageVariantId: images.endImageVariantId,
233	        pairShotGenerationId: task.pairShotGenerationId,
234	        projectResolution: task.projectResolution,
235	        modelName: task.modelName,
236	        modelType: policy.travelMode,
237	        ...(continuationEnabled
238	          ? {
239	            continuationConfig: {
240	              strategy: policy.continuation.strategy!,
241	              overlap_frames: policy.continuation.overlapFrames,
242	            },
243	            frameOverlapFromPrevious: policy.continuation.overlapFrames,
244	          }
245	          : {
246	            frameOverlapFromPrevious: 0,
247	          }),
248	        ...(enhancedPromptParam ? { enhancedPrompt: enhancedPromptParam } : {}),
249	        ...(task.structureInput?.travelGuidance ? { travelGuidance: task.structureInput.travelGuidance } : {}),
250	        skipMotionFields: !spec.supportsMotionFields,
251	        originalParams: task.originalParams,
252	      },
253	    );
254	  };

64	/**
65	 * Hook for managing Img2Img mode state and generation
66	 * Uses Z Image Turbo I2I task type with full LoRA selector support
67	 * 
68	 * Strength, enablePromptExpansion, and prompt are persisted via editSettingsPersistence
69	 * Prompt is persisted per-generation (shared with other edit modes, never inherited)
70	 */
71	export const useImg2ImgMode = ({
72	  media,
73	  selectedProjectId,
74	  isVideo,
75	  availableLoras = [],
76	  state,
77	  source,
78	  options,
79	}: UseImg2ImgModeProps): UseImg2ImgModeReturn => {
80	  const {
81	    strength: img2imgStrength,
82	    setStrength: setImg2imgStrength,
83	    enablePromptExpansion,
84	    setEnablePromptExpansion,
85	    prompt: img2imgPrompt,
86	    setPrompt: setImg2imgPrompt,
87	    promptHasBeenSet: img2imgPromptHasBeenSet,
88	    numGenerations,
89	  } = state;
90	  const { baseImageUrl, activeVariantLocation, activeVariantId, shotId } = source;
91	  const { toolTypeOverride, createAsGeneration } = options ?? {};
92	
93	  // Local state (not persisted)
94	  const [isGeneratingImg2Img, setIsGeneratingImg2Img] = useState(false);
95	  const [img2imgGenerateSuccess, setImg2imgGenerateSuccess] = useState(false);
96	  const run = useTaskPlaceholder();
97	
98	  // Derive the base generation prompt from the generation params (best-effort)
99	  const baseGenerationPrompt = useMemo(() => {
100	    const params = media.params;
101	    const raw =
102	      (typeof params?.base_prompt === 'string' && params.base_prompt) ||
103	      (typeof params?.prompt === 'string' && params.prompt) ||
104	      '';
105	    return raw.trim();
106	  }, [media]);
107	
108	  // Default Img2Img prompt to the prompt that generated the base image (one-time per generation)
109	  useEffect(() => {
110	    if (img2imgPromptHasBeenSet) return;
111	    if (img2imgPrompt && img2imgPrompt.trim().length > 0) return;
112	    if (!baseGenerationPrompt) return;
113	
114	    setImg2imgPrompt(baseGenerationPrompt);
115	  }, [img2imgPromptHasBeenSet, img2imgPrompt, baseGenerationPrompt, setImg2imgPrompt]);
116	
117	  // Use the shared LoRA manager hook
118	  const loraManager = useLoraManager(availableLoras, {
119	    projectId: selectedProjectId || undefined,
120	    persistenceScope: 'none', // Don't persist for img2img - it's a quick tool
121	    enableProjectPersistence: false,
122	    disableAutoLoad: true,
123	  });
124	
125	  // Track generation to prevent double-submits
126	  const isSubmittingRef = useRef(false);
127	
128	  const handleGenerateImg2Img = useCallback(async () => {
129	    // Validate inputs
130	    if (!selectedProjectId) {
131	      toast.error('No project selected');
132	      return;
133	    }
134	
135	    if (isVideo) {
136	      toast.error('Img2Img is only available for images');
137	      return;
138	    }
139	
140	    if (!baseImageUrl && !activeVariantLocation) {
141	      toast.error('No source image URL available');
142	      return;
143	    }
144	
145	    // Prevent double-submits
146	    if (isSubmittingRef.current) {
147	      return;
148	    }
149	
150	    isSubmittingRef.current = true;
151	    setIsGeneratingImg2Img(true);
152	
153	    try {
154	      await run({
155	        taskType: 'z_image_turbo_i2i',
156	        label: img2imgPrompt.trim() || 'Img2Img...',
157	        context: 'useImg2ImgMode',
158	        toastTitle: 'Failed to create Img2Img tasks',
159	        create: () => {
160	          // Convert selected LoRAs to the format expected by the task
161	          const loras: FalLoraConfig[] = loraManager.selectedLoras.map((lora: ActiveLora) => ({
162	            path: lora.path,
163	            scale: lora.strength,
164	          }));
165	
166	          // Use active variant's location if editing a variant, otherwise use the base image URL
167	          const effectiveImageUrl = activeVariantLocation || baseImageUrl;
168	
169	          // Get actual generation ID (handle shot_generations case)
170	          const actualGenerationId = getGenerationId(media);
171	
172	          return createTask({
173	            project_id: selectedProjectId,
174	            family: 'z_image_turbo_i2i',
175	            input: {
176	              image_url: effectiveImageUrl,
177	              prompt: img2imgPrompt.trim() || undefined,
178	              strength: img2imgStrength,
179	              enable_prompt_expansion: enablePromptExpansion,
180	              numImages: numGenerations,
181	              loras: loras.length > 0 ? loras : undefined,
182	              based_on: actualGenerationId ?? undefined,
183	              source_variant_id: activeVariantId || undefined,
184	              create_as_generation: createAsGeneration,
185	              tool_type: toolTypeOverride,
186	              shot_id: shotId,
187	            },
188	          });
189	        },
190	        onSuccess: () => {
191	          setImg2imgGenerateSuccess(true);
192	          setTimeout(() => {
193	            setImg2imgGenerateSuccess(false);
194	          }, 2000);
195	        },
196	      });
197	    } finally {
198	      setIsGeneratingImg2Img(false);
199	      isSubmittingRef.current = false;
200	    }
201	  }, [
202	    selectedProjectId,
203	    isVideo,
204	    baseImageUrl,
205	    activeVariantLocation,
206	    activeVariantId,
207	    media,
208	    img2imgPrompt,
209	    img2imgStrength,
210	    enablePromptExpansion,
211	    numGenerations,
212	    loraManager.selectedLoras,
213	    createAsGeneration,
214	    toolTypeOverride,
215	    shotId,
216	    run,
217	  ]);
218	
219	  return {
220	    // State
221	    img2imgPrompt,
222	    img2imgStrength,
223	    enablePromptExpansion,
224	    isGeneratingImg2Img,
225	    img2imgGenerateSuccess,
226	
227	    // Setters
228	    setImg2imgPrompt,
229	    setImg2imgStrength,
230	    setEnablePromptExpansion,
231	
232	    // LoRA Manager
233	    loraManager,
234	
235	    // Actions
236	    handleGenerateImg2Img,
237	  };
238	};

15	/**
16	 * Low-level hook for creating image generation tasks.
17	 *
18	 * NOTE: This hook does NOT manage incoming task placeholders. The caller
19	 * (useFormSubmission → useSubmitHandler → runIncomingTask) already wraps
20	 * the call in a placeholder lifecycle. Adding a second placeholder here
21	 * would cause double-counting in the TasksPane.
22	 */
23	export function useImageGenSubmit({
24	  projectId,
25	  effectiveProjectId,
26	}: UseImageGenSubmitParams) {
27	  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
28	  const { getApiKey } = useApiKeys();
29	
30	  const handleNewGenerate = useCallback(async (taskParams: BatchImageGenerationTaskParams): Promise<string[]> => {
31	    if (!projectId) {
32	      toast.error("No project selected. Please select a project before generating images.");
33	      return [];
34	    }
35	
36	    try {
37	      const { project_id, ...input } = taskParams;
38	      const createdTasks = await createTask({
39	        project_id,
40	        family: 'image_generation',
41	        input,
42	      });
43	      const createdTaskIds = createdTasks.task_ids ?? [createdTasks.task_id];
44	
45	      // Refresh the gallery/media view. Task pane invalidation is handled by the
46	      // caller's runIncomingTask placeholder (awaited refetch + placeholder cleanup).
47	      // Doing fire-and-forget task invalidation here would race with the placeholder
48	      // and cause cancelled tasks to flash briefly in the UI.
49	      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED](effectiveProjectId) });
50	
51	      return createdTaskIds;
52	    } catch (error) {
53	      if (import.meta.env.DEV) {
54	        console.error('[handleNewGenerate] FAILED:', error);
55	      }
56	      normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'ImageGenerationToolPage.handleNewGenerate', toastTitle: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Failed to create tasks.' });
57	      return [];
58	    }
59	  }, [projectId, effectiveProjectId, queryClient]);
60	
61	  const openaiApiKey = getApiKey('openai_api_key');
62	
63	  return {
64	    handleNewGenerate,
65	    openaiApiKey,
66	  };
67	}

2	import { GenerationRow } from '@/domains/generation/types';

4	import { getGenerationId, getMediaUrl } from '@/shared/lib/media/mediaTypeHelpers';
5	import type { ImageUpscaleSettings } from '../components/ImageUpscaleForm';
6	import { useTaskPlaceholder } from '@/shared/hooks/tasks/useTaskPlaceholder';
7	
8	interface UseUpscaleProps {
9	  media: GenerationRow | undefined;
10	  selectedProjectId: string | null;
11	  isVideo: boolean;
12	  shotId?: string;
13	}
14	
15	interface UseUpscaleReturn {
16	  isUpscaling: boolean;
17	  upscaleSuccess: boolean;
18	  handleUpscale: (settings: ImageUpscaleSettings) => Promise<void>;
19	  /** Update the active variant info so handleUpscale uses the correct image.
20	   *  Call this after variant data becomes available (e.g. from useSharedLightboxState). */
21	  setActiveVariant: (location: string | null | undefined, id: string | null | undefined) => void;
22	  effectiveImageUrl: string;
23	}
24	
25	/**
26	 * Hook for managing image upscaling functionality
27	 *
28	 * Simple pattern matching other edit tasks (inpaint, etc.):
29	 * 1. Click button → isUpscaling = true
30	 * 2. Task created → upscaleSuccess = true briefly
31	 * 3. Reset after timeout
32	 *
33	 * Variant tracking: call setActiveVariant() after variant data is available
34	 * so handleUpscale upscales the currently-viewed variant (not the base generation).
35	 */
36	export const useUpscale = ({
37	  media,
38	  selectedProjectId,
39	  isVideo,
40	  shotId,
41	}: UseUpscaleProps): UseUpscaleReturn => {
42	  const [isUpscaling, setIsUpscaling] = useState(false);
43	  const [upscaleSuccess, setUpscaleSuccess] = useState(false);
44	  const run = useTaskPlaceholder();
45	
46	  // Get media URL
47	  const mediaUrl = media ? (getMediaUrl(media) || media.imageUrl || '') : '';
48	
49	  // Refs for active variant info — set via setActiveVariant after variant data loads.
50	  // Using refs so the handleUpscale callback always reads the latest values
51	  // without needing them in useCallback deps (avoids hook-ordering issues).
52	  const activeVariantLocationRef = useRef<string | null | undefined>(null);
53	  const activeVariantIdRef = useRef<string | null | undefined>(null);
54	
55	  const setActiveVariant = useCallback((location: string | null | undefined, id: string | null | undefined) => {
56	    activeVariantLocationRef.current = location;
57	    activeVariantIdRef.current = id;
58	  }, []);
59	
60	  const handleUpscale = useCallback(async (settings: ImageUpscaleSettings) => {
61	    if (!media || !selectedProjectId || isVideo) {
62	      return;
63	    }
64	
65	    // Use active variant's location if viewing a variant, otherwise use base generation URL
66	    const activeVariantLocation = activeVariantLocationRef.current;
67	    const activeVariantId = activeVariantIdRef.current;
68	    const effectiveImageUrl = activeVariantLocation || mediaUrl;
69	
70	    setIsUpscaling(true);
71	    try {
72	      await run({
73	        taskType: 'image-upscale',
74	        label: `Upscale ${settings.scaleFactor}x`,
75	        context: 'useUpscale',
76	        toastTitle: 'Failed to create enhance task',
77	        create: async () => {
78	          if (!effectiveImageUrl) {
79	            throw new Error('No image URL available');
80	          }
81	
82	          const actualGenerationId = getGenerationId(media);
83	
84	          return createTask({
85	            project_id: selectedProjectId,
86	            family: 'image_upscale',
87	            input: {
88	              image_url: effectiveImageUrl,
89	              generation_id: actualGenerationId,
90	              source_variant_id: activeVariantId || undefined,
91	              scale_factor: settings.scaleFactor,
92	              noise_scale: settings.noiseScale,
93	              shot_id: shotId,
94	            },
95	          });
96	        },
97	        onSuccess: () => {
98	          // Show success state briefly
99	          setUpscaleSuccess(true);
100	          setTimeout(() => {
101	            setUpscaleSuccess(false);
102	          }, 2000);
103	        },
104	      });
105	    } finally {
106	      setIsUpscaling(false);
107	    }
108	  }, [media, selectedProjectId, isVideo, mediaUrl, shotId, run]);
109	
110	  return useMemo(
111	    () => ({
112	      isUpscaling,
113	      upscaleSuccess,
114	      handleUpscale,
115	      setActiveVariant,
116	      effectiveImageUrl: mediaUrl,
117	    }),
118	    [isUpscaling, upscaleSuccess, handleUpscale, setActiveVariant, mediaUrl],
119	  );
120	};
121

65	function deduplicateChildGenerations(children: GenerationRow[]): GenerationRow[] {
66	  const seenChildOrders = new Set<number>();
67	  return children.filter(child => {
68	    const rawChildOrder = child.child_order;
69	    if (rawChildOrder === undefined || rawChildOrder === null) return true;
70	
71	    const childOrder = typeof rawChildOrder === 'number'
72	      ? rawChildOrder
73	      : parseInt(String(rawChildOrder), 10);
74	
75	    if (Number.isNaN(childOrder)) return true;
76	    if (seenChildOrders.has(childOrder)) return false;
77	
78	    seenChildOrders.add(childOrder);
79	    return true;
80	  });
81	}

83	async function fetchChildGenerations(parentGenerationId: string): Promise<GenerationRow[]> {
84	  const { data, error } = await supabase().from('generations')
85	    .select('*')
86	    .eq('parent_generation_id', parentGenerationId)
87	    .order('child_order', { ascending: true })
88	    .order('created_at', { ascending: false });
89	
90	  if (error) throw error;
91	  if (!data) return [];
92	
93	  const mapped = data.map(gen => ({
94	    id: gen.id,

96	    imageUrl: gen.location || '',

102	    parent_generation_id: gen.parent_generation_id,
103	    child_order: gen.child_order,
104	  })) as GenerationRow[];
105	
106	  return deduplicateChildGenerations(mapped);
107	}

119	  const resolutionMap = useLtxHd ? LTX_ASPECT_RATIO_TO_RESOLUTION : ASPECT_RATIO_TO_RESOLUTION;
120	  if (selectedShot?.aspect_ratio) {
121	    const shotResolution = resolutionMap[selectedShot.aspect_ratio];
122	    if (shotResolution) return shotResolution;
123	  }
124	  if (effectiveAspectRatio) {
125	    const projectResolution = resolutionMap[effectiveAspectRatio];
126	    if (projectResolution) return projectResolution;
127	  }
128	  return useLtxHd ? '1280x720' : DEFAULT_RESOLUTION;
129	}

131	async function waitForPendingMutations(queryClient: QueryClient, timeoutMs = 5000): Promise<void> {
132	  if (queryClient.isMutating() === 0) return;
133	
134	  const start = Date.now();
135	  while (queryClient.isMutating() > 0) {
136	    if (Date.now() - start > timeoutMs) break;
137	    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 50));
138	  }
139	}

141	async function fetchFreshShotGenerations(selectedShotId: string): Promise<ShotGenRow[]> {
142	  const { data, error } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
143	    .select(SHOT_GEN_QUERY)
144	    .eq('shot_id', selectedShotId)
145	    .order('timeline_frame', { ascending: true });
146	
147	  if (error) throw error;
148	  return (data || []) as ShotGenRow[];

151	async function persistEnhancedPromptsMetadata(
152	  shotId: string,
153	  queryClient: QueryClient,
154	  allShotGenerations: ShotGenRow[],
155	  enhancedPrompts: string[],
156	): Promise<void> {
157	  if (enhancedPrompts.length === 0) {
158	    return;
159	  }
160	
161	  const sourceShotGenerations = filterImageShotGenerations(allShotGenerations)
162	    .slice(0, enhancedPrompts.length);
163	
164	  if (sourceShotGenerations.length === 0) {
165	    return;
166	  }
167	
168	  const metadataUpdates = sourceShotGenerations.map((shotGeneration, index) => ({
169	    shotGenerationId: shotGeneration.id,
170	    metadata: {
171	      ...((shotGeneration.metadata as Record<string, unknown> | null) || {}),
172	      enhanced_prompt: enhancedPrompts[index] ?? '',
173	    },
174	  }));
175	
176	  const metadataByShotGenerationId = new Map(
177	    metadataUpdates.map((update) => [update.shotGenerationId, update.metadata]),
178	  );
179	
180	  queryClient.setQueryData<GenerationRow[]>(
181	    queryKeys.generations.byShot(shotId),
182	    (oldData) => oldData?.map((row) => {
183	      const updatedMetadata = metadataByShotGenerationId.get(row.id);
184	      return updatedMetadata
185	        ? { ...row, metadata: updatedMetadata }
186	        : row;
187	    }),
188	  );
189	
190	  const results = await Promise.all(metadataUpdates.map((update) =>
191	    supabase().from('shot_generations')
192	      .update({ metadata: toJson(update.metadata) })
193	      .eq('id', update.shotGenerationId),
194	  ));
195	
196	  const firstError = results.find((result) => result.error)?.error;
197	  if (firstError) {
198	    await Promise.all([
199	      queryClient.refetchQueries({ [REDACTED](shotId) }),
200	      queryClient.refetchQueries({ [REDACTED](shotId) }),
201	    ]);
202	    throw firstError;
203	  }
204	
205	  await Promise.all([
206	    queryClient.refetchQueries({ [REDACTED](shotId) }),
207	    queryClient.refetchQueries({ [REDACTED](shotId) }),
208	    ...metadataUpdates.map((update) =>
209	      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED](update.shotGenerationId) })),
210	  ]);
211	}

247	export async function generateVideo(params: GenerateVideoParams): Promise<GenerateVideoResult> {
248	  const {

268	
269	  if (!projectId) {
270	    return failureResult(

272	      { context: 'generateVideoService', toastTitle: 'No project selected' },
273	    );
274	  }
275	
276	  await waitForPendingMutations(queryClient);
277	  const spec = getModelSpec(modelConfig.selectedModel);
278	  const policy = resolveGenerationPolicy(spec, {
279	    smoothContinuations: modelConfig.smoothContinuations ?? false,
280	    requestedExecutionMode: modelConfig.generation_type_mode ?? 'i2v',
281	    guidanceKind: resolveGuidanceKind(travelGuidance),
282	    hasStructureVideo: structureVideos.length > 0,
283	  });
284	  const useLtxHd = spec.modelFamily === 'ltx' && modelConfig.ltxHdResolution !== false;
285	  const resolution = resolveGenerationResolution(selectedShot, effectiveAspectRatio, useLtxHd);
286	  const amountOfMotion = motionConfig.amount_of_motion ?? 50;
287	  const effectiveBatchVideoFrames = clampFrameCountToPolicy(batchVideoFrames, spec, {
288	    smoothContinuations: modelConfig.smoothContinuations ?? false,
289	    requestedExecutionMode: modelConfig.generation_type_mode ?? 'i2v',
290	    guidanceKind: resolveGuidanceKind(travelGuidance),
291	    hasStructureVideo: structureVideos.length > 0,
292	  });
293	
294	  let allShotGenerations: ShotGenRow[];
295	  try {
296	    allShotGenerations = await fetchFreshShotGenerations(selectedShotId);
297	  } catch (error) {
298	    return failureResult(error, {
299	      context: 'TaskSubmission',
300	      toastTitle: 'Failed to fetch current images',
301	    });
302	  }
303	
304	  const imagePayload = buildImagePayload(allShotGenerations);
305	  const pairConfig = (() => {
306	    switch (generationMode) {
307	      case 'timeline':
308	        return buildTimelinePairConfig(allShotGenerations, effectiveBatchVideoFrames, promptConfig.default_negative_prompt, policy.frameOverlap);
309	      case 'by-pair':
310	        return buildByPairConfig(allShotGenerations, effectiveBatchVideoFrames, promptConfig.default_negative_prompt, policy.frameOverlap);
311	      case 'batch':
312	      default:
313	        return buildBatchPairConfig(imagePayload.absoluteImageUrls, effectiveBatchVideoFrames, promptConfig.default_negative_prompt, policy.frameOverlap);
314	    }
315	  })();
316	
317	  if (promptConfig.enhance_prompt) {
318	    try {
319	      pairConfig.enhancedPromptsArray = await enhancePromptsForBatch({
320	        batchBasePrompt: promptConfig.base_prompt,
321	        pairCount: pairConfig.basePrompts.length,
322	        pairOverridePrompts: pairConfig.basePrompts,
323	        numFrames: pairConfig.segmentFrames[0],

325	        signal: promptConfig.enhancementAbortSignal,
326	      });
327	
328	      try {
329	        await persistEnhancedPromptsMetadata(
330	          selectedShotId,

332	          allShotGenerations,
333	          pairConfig.enhancedPromptsArray.map((prompt) => prompt ?? ''),
334	        );
335	      } catch (persistError) {
336	        normalizeAndPresentError(persistError, {
337	          context: 'generateVideoService.persistEnhancedPromptsMetadata',
338	          showToast: false,

342	      return failureResult(error, {

344	        toastTitle: 'Failed to enhance prompts',

347	    }
348

418	  }

# Local-only generations as worker task inputs

Read CLAUDE.md at the repo root first — it has cross-cutting rules and points to relevant sub-docs (especially `task_worker_lifecycle.md`, `unified_task_creation.md`, `storage_uploads.md`, `edge_functions.md`).

## Background

The app now supports `storage_mode='local'` generations (see `src/shared/lib/media/createGenerationFromFile.ts` → `createGenerationForLocalFile()`). The bytes live in the user's browser via a `FileSystemFileHandle` persisted in IndexedDB; the DB row carries `local_handle_id` instead of a `location` URL.

Today, when a user takes a generation and uses it as **input** to a worker task (travel, refine, masked-edit, etc.), the app puts a Supabase Storage URL into task params and the worker fetches it via HTTP. For local-only generations, that URL doesn't exist — and the worker has no way to reach into the browser.

This task wires those local-only generations through to the worker correctly, with a tiered strategy.

## Design

Implement a **per-input** resolution layer that runs at task-create time. For each input that references a generation:

1. If `storage_mode === 'remote'` (or absent / 'uploading' that has materialized) → use existing URL behavior. No change.
2. If `storage_mode === 'local'`:
   - **Detect whether a local worker is reachable** via a healthcheck (e.g. `GET http://localhost:<configured-port>/health` with a short timeout, ~250ms). Cache the answer for the duration of the task-creation call (don't re-probe per input).
   - **If local worker reachable**: read the file bytes from the FileSystemFileHandle, write them to a known shared dir (e.g. `~/.reigh-local-files/<local_handle_id>.<ext>`), and put a `file://` URL pointing at that path into the task params. The worker's `download_utils.py` already handles `file://` URLs (verify this — `reigh-worker/source/utils/download_utils.py` around line 60), so no worker changes should be needed. The materialized file is the "duplicate" per user wording.
   - **If no local worker**: upload the file bytes to Supabase Storage on demand. Reuse the existing upload helper in `src/shared/lib/media/imageUploader.ts`. Put the resulting public URL into task params. Mark the generation row with the new `location` (or a sibling `materialized_location`) so a second use of the same input doesn't re-upload — idempotent.

## Mixed inputs

A single task can reference both local-only and remote generations as inputs. The resolver MUST operate per-input, not per-task. After resolution, the task params contain a uniform set of URL strings (mix of `https://...` and `file://...`) — the worker doesn't know or care which inputs were originally local.

## Cleanup ("delete the duplicate after")

After task completion, the duplicate created during resolution must be cleaned up so we don't accumulate orphaned copies:

- **Local-worker `file://` materialization**: when the task completes, the file at `~/.reigh-local-files/<handle_id>.<ext>` is no longer needed. Delete it. Implement this in the `complete_task` edge function path OR via a worker-side cleanup hook OR via an app-side post-completion handler — whichever is most natural given the existing complete-task lifecycle. The original FileSystemFileHandle in the browser is untouched; we only delete the materialized copy.
- **Remote-worker upload-on-demand**: this is more nuanced. If we keep the uploaded copy, the generation effectively becomes remote-mode, defeating the user's local choice. Recommended: keep the upload only for the duration of the task (idempotency caching) and delete it after task completion. Update the generation row to remove the cached URL. Same lifecycle hook as above. If the user uses the same local generation as input again later, we re-upload (small cost, preserves intent).

The lifecycle hook should look at the resolved task params, identify which entries were materializations of local generations (mark them at creation time so cleanup knows), and clean each up. Don't touch generations that were natively remote.

## Detection of local worker

The localhost healthcheck endpoint and port: check existing reigh-worker server entrypoint (`reigh-worker/source/runtime/worker/server.py`) for the actual healthcheck route + port. If none exists, you'll need to add a tiny `/health` endpoint to the worker (returns 200 OK + JSON `{ok:true}`). Keep this minimal.

The app also needs to know which port to probe — read it from an env var (`VITE_LOCAL_WORKER_HEALTHCHECK_URL` or similar), default to a sensible value. Don't hard-code.

If the healthcheck fails (timeout, connection refused), fall back to remote behavior. Don't surface an error to the user — silent fallback is correct UX.

## Where to put the resolution layer

There's a unified task-creation path in `src/shared/lib/tasks/`. Look for the common entry point (probably a hook like `useCreateTask` or a shared `createTask` helper). The resolver should run there, immediately before the create-task edge function call. Sub-doc `unified_task_creation.md` is authoritative — read it first.

For tasks that build their own params (e.g. `src/shared/lib/tasks/travelBetweenImages/segmentImages.ts`, `src/shared/lib/tasks/imageEditing/buildMaskedEditTaskParams.ts`), the resolver needs a hook into each. Consider whether the resolver runs at the very end of param assembly (one place to plug in) or whether each task builder calls it explicitly. The first option is simpler and harder to forget.

## What NOT to do

- Do NOT make the worker do FileSystemFileHandle deserialization. Browser handles can't cross processes.
- Do NOT eagerly upload all local files at drop time. That defeats the point — only materialize on USE.
- Do NOT add a "this will be uploaded to cloud, OK?" prompt. The fallback should be silent. (We can add UX later if needed.)
- Do NOT refactor the unified task-creation system. Plug into it.
- Do NOT add comments explaining the change. The diff speaks for itself.

## Tests

- Add tests for the resolver covering: all-remote inputs (passthrough), all-local + local worker present (file:// path), all-local + remote only (upload + cache), mixed inputs (per-input branching), cleanup after completion.
- Mock the healthcheck and the upload helper. Don't hit real network.
- Mirror existing test patterns in `src/shared/lib/tasks/__tests__/` or wherever co-located tests live.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` — must not introduce new errors beyond pre-existing patterns.
- `npx vitest run` for affected directories.
- Manually trace through one task type (travel-between-images is a good one) to verify the resolver runs and the URL contract holds.

## Deliverables

- The per-input resolver, wired into the unified task-creation path.
- Local-worker healthcheck utility.
- Cleanup hook on task completion.
- A `/health` endpoint on the worker if one doesn't exist.
- Tests covering the matrix above.
- Brief summary in your final message: every task type touched, every caller of the create-task path you verified.

# Local-only generations as worker task inputs

Read CLAUDE.md at the repo root first — it has cross-cutting rules and points to relevant sub-docs (especially `task_worker_lifecycle.md`, `unified_task_creation.md`, `storage_uploads.md`, `edge_functions.md`).

## Background

The app now supports `storage_mode='local'` generations (see `src/shared/lib/media/createGenerationFromFile.ts` → `createGenerationForLocalFile()`). The bytes live in the user's browser via a `FileSystemFileHandle` persisted in IndexedDB; the DB row carries `local_handle_id` instead of a `location` URL.

Today, when a user takes a generation and uses it as **input** to a worker task (travel, refine, masked-edit, etc.), the app puts a Supabase Storage URL into task params and the worker fetches it via HTTP. For local-only generations, that URL doesn't exist — and the worker has no way to reach into the browser.

This task wires those local-only generations through to the worker correctly, with a tiered strategy.

## Design

Implement a **per-input** resolution layer that runs at task-create time. For each input that references a generation:

1. If `storage_mode === 'remote'` (or absent / 'uploading' that has materialized) → use existing URL behavior. No change.
2. If `storage_mode === 'local'`:
   - **Detect whether a local worker is reachable** via a healthcheck (e.g. `GET http://localhost:<configured-port>/health` with a short timeout, ~250ms). Cache the answer for the duration of the task-creation call (don't re-probe per input).
   - **If local worker reachable**: read the file bytes from the FileSystemFileHandle, write them to a known shared dir (e.g. `~/.reigh-local-files/<local_handle_id>.<ext>`), and put a `file://` URL pointing at that path into the task params. The worker's `download_utils.py` already handles `file://` URLs (verify this — `reigh-worker/source/utils/download_utils.py` around line 60), so no worker changes should be needed. The materialized file is the "duplicate" per user wording.
   - **If no local worker**: upload the file bytes to Supabase Storage on demand. Reuse the existing upload helper in `src/shared/lib/media/imageUploader.ts`. Put the resulting public URL into task params. Mark the generation row with the new `location` (or a sibling `materialized_location`) so a second use of the same input doesn't re-upload — idempotent.

## Mixed inputs

A single task can reference both local-only and remote generations as inputs. The resolver MUST operate per-input, not per-task. After resolution, the task params contain a uniform set of URL strings (mix of `https://...` and `file://...`) — the worker doesn't know or care which inputs were originally local.

## Cleanup ("delete the duplicate after")

After task completion, the duplicate created during resolution must be cleaned up so we don't accumulate orphaned copies:

- **Local-worker `file://` materialization**: when the task completes, the file at `~/.reigh-local-files/<handle_id>.<ext>` is no longer needed. Delete it. Implement this in the `complete_task` edge function path OR via a worker-side cleanup hook OR via an app-side post-completion handler — whichever is most natural given the existing complete-task lifecycle. The original FileSystemFileHandle in the browser is untouched; we only delete the materialized copy.
- **Remote-worker upload-on-demand**: this is more nuanced. If we keep the uploaded copy, the generation effectively becomes remote-mode, defeating the user's local choice. Recommended: keep the upload only for the duration of the task (idempotency caching) and delete it after task completion. Update the generation row to remove the cached URL. Same lifecycle hook as above. If the user uses the same local generation as input again later, we re-upload (small cost, preserves intent).

The lifecycle hook should look at the resolved task params, identify which entries were materializations of local generations (mark them at creation time so cleanup knows), and clean each up. Don't touch generations that were natively remote.

## Detection of local worker

The localhost healthcheck endpoint and port: check existing reigh-worker server entrypoint (`reigh-worker/source/runtime/worker/server.py`) for the actual healthcheck route + port. If none exists, you'll need to add a tiny `/health` endpoint to the worker (returns 200 OK + JSON `{ok:true}`). Keep this minimal.

The app also needs to know which port to probe — read it from an env var (`VITE_LOCAL_WORKER_HEALTHCHECK_URL` or similar), default to a sensible value. Don't hard-code.

If the healthcheck fails (timeout, connection refused), fall back to remote behavior. Don't surface an error to the user — silent fallback is correct UX.

## Where to put the resolution layer

There's a unified task-creation path in `src/shared/lib/tasks/`. Look for the common entry point (probably a hook like `useCreateTask` or a shared `createTask` helper). The resolver should run there, immediately before the create-task edge function call. Sub-doc `unified_task_creation.md` is authoritative — read it first.

For tasks that build their own params (e.g. `src/shared/lib/tasks/travelBetweenImages/segmentImages.ts`, `src/shared/lib/tasks/imageEditing/buildMaskedEditTaskParams.ts`), the resolver needs a hook into each. Consider whether the resolver runs at the very end of param assembly (one place to plug in) or whether each task builder calls it explicitly. The first option is simpler and harder to forget.

## What NOT to do

- Do NOT make the worker do FileSystemFileHandle deserialization. Browser handles can't cross processes.
- Do NOT eagerly upload all local files at drop time. That defeats the point — only materialize on USE.
- Do NOT add a "this will be uploaded to cloud, OK?" prompt. The fallback should be silent. (We can add UX later if needed.)
- Do NOT refactor the unified task-creation system. Plug into it.
- Do NOT add comments explaining the change. The diff speaks for itself.

## Tests

- Add tests for the resolver covering: all-remote inputs (passthrough), all-local + local worker present (file:// path), all-local + remote only (upload + cache), mixed inputs (per-input branching), cleanup after completion.
- Mock the healthcheck and the upload helper. Don't hit real network.
- Mirror existing test patterns in `src/shared/lib/tasks/__tests__/` or wherever co-located tests live.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` — must not introduce new errors beyond pre-existing patterns.
- `npx vitest run` for affected directories.
- Manually trace through one task type (travel-between-images is a good one) to verify the resolver runs and the URL contract holds.

## Deliverables

- The per-input resolver, wired into the unified task-creation path.
- Local-worker healthcheck utility.
- Cleanup hook on task completion.
- A `/health` endpoint on the worker if one doesn't exist.
- Tests covering the matrix above.

(flagged 2 times across 1 plans)

(flagged 2 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the render-gating cleanup plan against remotion's runtime exports in `node_modules/remotion/dist/cjs/cancel-render.js:46-70`. `cancelrender()` stores an error and throws to abort the render; it is not a benign cleanup for an abandoned `delayrender` handle, so step 2's instruction to call `cancelrender(handle)` on unmount is technically wrong and would abort preview or export with an error. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked how remotion itself acquires delay handles in `node_modules/remotion/dist/cjs/iframe.js:8-18`. remotion's own components create the handle synchronously with `usestate(() => delayrender(...))`; the plan says 'calls delayrender() on mount', which reads like an effect-time action and leaves the initial-frame blocking behavior underspecified compared with the actual library pattern. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the new `useaudioparam()` sketch against `src/tools/video-editor/effects/compileeffect.tsx:1-2`. the plan defines it in terms of `interpolate(audio[binding.source], ...)` but does not explicitly import `interpolate` into the new hook file or simplify it to straight arithmetic, so the helper's implementation contract is still looser than it needs to be. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked revised step 2.4 against `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useclipresize.ts:76-100`. the plan still says to clamp audio by writing back to `action.end`, but the current hook treats the callback `action` as input data and then creates fresh row actions from it. mutating that caller-owned object is unnecessary and risks coupling the resize hook to outside references instead of using a local `clampedend` variable. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)

# Local-only generations as worker task inputs

Read CLAUDE.md at the repo root first — it has cross-cutting rules and points to relevant sub-docs (especially `task_worker_lifecycle.md`, `unified_task_creation.md`, `storage_uploads.md`, `edge_functions.md`).

## Background

The app now supports `storage_mode='local'` generations (see `src/shared/lib/media/createGenerationFromFile.ts` → `createGenerationForLocalFile()`). The bytes live in the user's browser via a `FileSystemFileHandle` persisted in IndexedDB; the DB row carries `local_handle_id` instead of a `location` URL.

Today, when a user takes a generation and uses it as **input** to a worker task (travel, refine, masked-edit, etc.), the app puts a Supabase Storage URL into task params and the worker fetches it via HTTP. For local-only generations, that URL doesn't exist — and the worker has no way to reach into the browser.

This task wires those local-only generations through to the worker correctly, with a tiered strategy.

## Design

Implement a **per-input** resolution layer that runs at task-create time. For each input that references a generation:

1. If `storage_mode === 'remote'` (or absent / 'uploading' that has materialized) → use existing URL behavior. No change.
2. If `storage_mode === 'local'`:
   - **Detect whether a local worker is reachable** via a healthcheck (e.g. `GET http://localhost:<configured-port>/health` with a short timeout, ~250ms). Cache the answer for the duration of the task-creation call (don't re-probe per input).
   - **If local worker reachable**: read the file bytes from the FileSystemFileHandle, write them to a known shared dir (e.g. `~/.reigh-local-files/<local_handle_id>.<ext>`), and put a `file://` URL pointing at that path into the task params. The worker's `download_utils.py` already handles `file://` URLs (verify this — `reigh-worker/source/utils/download_utils.py` around line 60), so no worker changes should be needed. The materialized file is the "duplicate" per user wording.
   - **If no local worker**: upload the file bytes to Supabase Storage on demand. Reuse the existing upload helper in `src/shared/lib/media/imageUploader.ts`. Put the resulting public URL into task params. Mark the generation row with the new `location` (or a sibling `materialized_location`) so a second use of the same input doesn't re-upload — idempotent.

## Mixed inputs

A single task can reference both local-only and remote generations as inputs. The resolver MUST operate per-input, not per-task. After resolution, the task params contain a uniform set of URL strings (mix of `https://...` and `file://...`) — the worker doesn't know or care which inputs were originally local.

## Cleanup ("delete the duplicate after")

After task completion, the duplicate created during resolution must be cleaned up so we don't accumulate orphaned copies:

- **Local-worker `file://` materialization**: when the task completes, the file at `~/.reigh-local-files/<handle_id>.<ext>` is no longer needed. Delete it. Implement this in the `complete_task` edge function path OR via a worker-side cleanup hook OR via an app-side post-completion handler — whichever is most natural given the existing complete-task lifecycle. The original FileSystemFileHandle in the browser is untouched; we only delete the materialized copy.
- **Remote-worker upload-on-demand**: this is more nuanced. If we keep the uploaded copy, the generation effectively becomes remote-mode, defeating the user's local choice. Recommended: keep the upload only for the duration of the task (idempotency caching) and delete it after task completion. Update the generation row to remove the cached URL. Same lifecycle hook as above. If the user uses the same local generation as input again later, we re-upload (small cost, preserves intent).

The lifecycle hook should look at the resolved task params, identify which entries were materializations of local generations (mark them at creation time so cleanup knows), and clean each up. Don't touch generations that were natively remote.

## Detection of local worker

The localhost healthcheck endpoint and port: check existing reigh-worker server entrypoint (`reigh-worker/source/runtime/worker/server.py`) for the actual healthcheck route + port. If none exists, you'll need to add a tiny `/health` endpoint to the worker (returns 200 OK + JSON `{ok:true}`). Keep this minimal.

The app also needs to know which port to probe — read it from an env var (`VITE_LOCAL_WORKER_HEALTHCHECK_URL` or similar), default to a sensible value. Don't hard-code.

If the healthcheck fails (timeout, connection refused), fall back to remote behavior. Don't surface an error to the user — silent fallback is correct UX.

## Where to put the resolution layer

There's a unified task-creation path in `src/shared/lib/tasks/`. Look for the common entry point (probably a hook like `useCreateTask` or a shared `createTask` helper). The resolver should run there, immediately before the create-task edge function call. Sub-doc `unified_task_creation.md` is authoritative — read it first.

For tasks that build their own params (e.g. `src/shared/lib/tasks/travelBetweenImages/segmentImages.ts`, `src/shared/lib/tasks/imageEditing/buildMaskedEditTaskParams.ts`), the resolver needs a hook into each. Consider whether the resolver runs at the very end of param assembly (one place to plug in) or whether each task builder calls it explicitly. The first option is simpler and harder to forget.

## What NOT to do

- Do NOT make the worker do FileSystemFileHandle deserialization. Browser handles can't cross processes.
- Do NOT eagerly upload all local files at drop time. That defeats the point — only materialize on USE.
- Do NOT add a "this will be uploaded to cloud, OK?" prompt. The fallback should be silent. (We can add UX later if needed.)
- Do NOT refactor the unified task-creation system. Plug into it.
- Do NOT add comments explaining the change. The diff speaks for itself.

## Tests

- Add tests for the resolver covering: all-remote inputs (passthrough), all-local + local worker present (file:// path), all-local + remote only (upload + cache), mixed inputs (per-input branching), cleanup after completion.
- Mock the healthcheck and the upload helper. Don't hit real network.
- Mirror existing test patterns in `src/shared/lib/tasks/__tests__/` or wherever co-located tests live.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` — must not introduce new errors beyond pre-existing patterns.
- `npx vitest run` for affected directories.
- Manually trace through one task type (travel-between-images is a good one) to verify the resolver runs and the URL contract holds.

## Deliverables

- The per-input resolver, wired into the unified task-creation path.
- Local-worker healthcheck utility.
- Cleanup hook on task completion.
- A `/health` endpoint on the worker if one doesn't exist.

# Local-only generations as worker task inputs

Read CLAUDE.md at the repo root first — it has cross-cutting rules and points to relevant sub-docs (especially `task_worker_lifecycle.md`, `unified_task_creation.md`, `storage_uploads.md`, `edge_functions.md`).

## Background

The app now supports `storage_mode='local'` generations (see `src/shared/lib/media/createGenerationFromFile.ts` → `createGenerationForLocalFile()`). The bytes live in the user's browser via a `FileSystemFileHandle` persisted in IndexedDB; the DB row carries `local_handle_id` instead of a `location` URL.

Today, when a user takes a generation and uses it as **input** to a worker task (travel, refine, masked-edit, etc.), the app puts a Supabase Storage URL into task params and the worker fetches it via HTTP. For local-only generations, that URL doesn't exist — and the worker has no way to reach into the browser.

This task wires those local-only generations through to the worker correctly, with a tiered strategy.

## Design

Implement a **per-input** resolution layer that runs at task-create time. For each input that references a generation:

1. If `storage_mode === 'remote'` (or absent / 'uploading' that has materialized) → use existing URL behavior. No change.
2. If `storage_mode === 'local'`:
   - **Detect whether a local worker is reachable** via a healthcheck (e.g. `GET http://localhost:<configured-port>/health` with a short timeout, ~250ms). Cache the answer for the duration of the task-creation call (don't re-probe per input).
   - **If local worker reachable**: read the file bytes from the FileSystemFileHandle, write them to a known shared dir (e.g. `~/.reigh-local-files/<local_handle_id>.<ext>`), and put a `file://` URL pointing at that path into the task params. The worker's `download_utils.py` already handles `file://` URLs (verify this — `reigh-worker/source/utils/download_utils.py` around line 60), so no worker changes should be needed. The materialized file is the "duplicate" per user wording.
   - **If no local worker**: upload the file bytes to Supabase Storage on demand. Reuse the existing upload helper in `src/shared/lib/media/imageUploader.ts`. Put the resulting public URL into task params. Mark the generation row with the new `location` (or a sibling `materialized_location`) so a second use of the same input doesn't re-upload — idempotent.

## Mixed inputs

A single task can reference both local-only and remote generations as inputs. The resolver MUST operate per-input, not per-task. After resolution, the task params contain a uniform set of URL strings (mix of `https://...` and `file://...`) — the worker doesn't know or care which inputs were originally local.

## Cleanup ("delete the duplicate after")

After task completion, the duplicate created during resolution must be cleaned up so we don't accumulate orphaned copies:

- **Local-worker `file://` materialization**: when the task completes, the file at `~/.reigh-local-files/<handle_id>.<ext>` is no longer needed. Delete it. Implement this in the `complete_task` edge function path OR via a worker-side cleanup hook OR via an app-side post-completion handler — whichever is most natural given the existing complete-task lifecycle. The original FileSystemFileHandle in the browser is untouched; we only delete the materialized copy.
- **Remote-worker upload-on-demand**: this is more nuanced. If we keep the uploaded copy, the generation effectively becomes remote-mode, defeating the user's local choice. Recommended: keep the upload only for the duration of the task (idempotency caching) and delete it after task completion. Update the generation row to remove the cached URL. Same lifecycle hook as above. If the user uses the same local generation as input again later, we re-upload (small cost, preserves intent).

The lifecycle hook should look at the resolved task params, identify which entries were materializations of local generations (mark them at creation time so cleanup knows), and clean each up. Don't touch generations that were natively remote.

## Detection of local worker

The localhost healthcheck endpoint and port: check existing reigh-worker server entrypoint (`reigh-worker/source/runtime/worker/server.py`) for the actual healthcheck route + port. If none exists, you'll need to add a tiny `/health` endpoint to the worker (returns 200 OK + JSON `{ok:true}`). Keep this minimal.

The app also needs to know which port to probe — read it from an env var (`VITE_LOCAL_WORKER_HEALTHCHECK_URL` or similar), default to a sensible value. Don't hard-code.

If the healthcheck fails (timeout, connection refused), fall back to remote behavior. Don't surface an error to the user — silent fallback is correct UX.

## Where to put the resolution layer

There's a unified task-creation path in `src/shared/lib/tasks/`. Look for the common entry point (probably a hook like `useCreateTask` or a shared `createTask` helper). The resolver should run there, immediately before the create-task edge function call. Sub-doc `unified_task_creation.md` is authoritative — read it first.

For tasks that build their own params (e.g. `src/shared/lib/tasks/travelBetweenImages/segmentImages.ts`, `src/shared/lib/tasks/imageEditing/buildMaskedEditTaskParams.ts`), the resolver needs a hook into each. Consider whether the resolver runs at the very end of param assembly (one place to plug in) or whether each task builder calls it explicitly. The first option is simpler and harder to forget.

## What NOT to do

- Do NOT make the worker do FileSystemFileHandle deserialization. Browser handles can't cross processes.
- Do NOT eagerly upload all local files at drop time. That defeats the point — only materialize on USE.
- Do NOT add a "this will be uploaded to cloud, OK?" prompt. The fallback should be silent. (We can add UX later if needed.)
- Do NOT refactor the unified task-creation system. Plug into it.
- Do NOT add comments explaining the change. The diff speaks for itself.

## Tests

- Add tests for the resolver covering: all-remote inputs (passthrough), all-local + local worker present (file:// path), all-local + remote only (upload + cache), mixed inputs (per-input branching), cleanup after completion.
- Mock the healthcheck and the upload helper. Don't hit real network.
- Mirror existing test patterns in `src/shared/lib/tasks/__tests__/` or wherever co-located tests live.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` — must not introduce new errors beyond pre-existing patterns.
- `npx vitest run` for affected directories.
- Manually trace through one task type (travel-between-images is a good one) to verify the resolver runs and the URL contract holds.

## Deliverables

- The per-input resolver, wired into the unified task-creation path.
- Local-worker healthcheck utility.
- Cleanup hook on task completion.
- A `/health` endpoint on the worker if one doesn't exist.
- Tests covering the matrix above.
- Brief summary in your final message: every task type touched, every caller of the create-task path you verified.
